Getting a configuration issue with an SSH connection from `git`.  I'm just trying to add the R CMD check YAML (with `usethis::use_github_action_check_standard`) to the package, but `git` has been a litlte funky with this.  

I'm not sure this should cause an error as the underlying function in `usethis:::target_repo_spec` and then `usethis:::target_repo` eventually return the information necessary for a badge, which is called by `usethis:::github_remote_config`.  

Normally, if I'm using `usethis::use_github_actions_badge` I can pass `repo_spec` to override this and not get an error, but `usethis::use_github_action_check_standard` doesn't have a pass through for `repo_spec` (maybe the solution?)

title: feature request: allow `use_github()` to create "internal" repositories
description:
First of all, many thanks for this awesome package. I bumped into this use case a number of times and, as far as I can tell, this feature request doesn't seem to have been discussed previously. Apologies if it was and a conclusion not to implement `visibility` had been reached.

Currently the only option when using `use_github()` is to create either a `public` or `private` repository. For enterprise accounts, there often is a 3rd use case, namely to create an `internal` repo. This is `private` as far as the rest of the world is concerned, but `public` from the point of view of the members of the organisation.  

I think it might be a case of adding an argument named `visibility` with the possible values `"public"`, `"private"` or `"internal"` (keeping in line with the [GitHub POST request parameters](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/reference/repos#create-an-organization-repository--parameters)). The default value for this argument could be `"public"` or `NULL`. Moreover, as far as I understand, the [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/reference/repos) state `visibility` overrides `private` in case of conflict. What do you think?

The expected behaviour would be:

```r
# creates an "internal" repo
use_github(organisation =  "My_awesome_organisation", private = FALSE, visibility = "internal")

# creates an "internal" repo as visibility overrides "private"
use_github(organisation =  "My_awesome_organisation", private = TRUE, visibility = "internal")

# use_github should error when organisation = NULL and visibility = "internal"
use_github(visibility = "internal")
```

title: Default README mentioning installing from CRAN is potentially confusing for new package authors
description:
The default README issue template mentions the package can be installed from CRAN.
This can be confusing to first time package authors, and also users who encounter the readme without having the package actually submitted and approved.

It makes it seem like the package is (somehow) already on CRAN, just by adding the readme. Particularly if this step was done in combination with doing other things, like setting up CI, a package author could get a mistaken impression about the CRAN status of their package.

It will always be wrong for packages which are never submitted to CRAN (which may very well be the majority). It will also be incorrect at least temporarily when a package is first being developed and not yet on CRAN.

The alternative (just showing the devel installation instructions) is also problematic if the instructions are not changed when the package is submitted to CRAN.

But I think generally the authors who submit to CRAN are more capable of changing the installation instructions appropriately than first time R package authors many of whom many never submit a package to CRAN.

title: Change `rstudio_config_path()`
description:
What we currently have is wrong. According to @jmcphers, the IDE folks didn't realize rappdirs has(and official XDG docs suggest) distinct behavior for Mac and Linux. In hindsight, RStudio should probably be more like rappdirs.

But all we need to worry about in usethis is matching what the IDE actually does.

Official docs:

https://support.rstudio.com/hc/en-us/articles/200534577-Resetting-RStudio-Desktop-s-State
https://docs.rstudio.com/ide/desktop-pro/settings.html

The real solution is for RStudio to just tell us where they look:

https://github.com/rstudio/rstudioapi/issues/176

Research inspired by reviewing #1420, which should probably be superseded by the fix for this.

title: Generalizing `use_github_action()` with `use_github_file()`
description:
I'm very interested in the pattern used by `use_github_action()` as an alternative to `use_template()` when it makes sense to host files somewhere else (e.g. we want to make it easier to grab a file from R but don't necessarily want to host it in the package itself because it's useful for other purposes). 

I think it would be nice to refactor that internal code to a new exported function, e.g. `use_github_file()`, which could then be called by `use_github_action()`. The pattern for reading a file from GitHub is, thankfully, not that complex, but it's very useful. 

Happy to prepare a PR if it seems like it's worth exporting that code

title: Mention remotes in GitHub creds vignette?
description:
One issue that I've had in sending people to the GH creds vignette is that remotes doesn't yet support the git cred store approach used by gert and gh (https://github.com/r-lib/remotes/issues/587), a problem which we bump into quickly since we use private GH repos on our team.

Hopefully, this will be a non-issue soon, but is it worth mentioning (temporarily?) in the vignette that remotes doesn't yet support this approach?

title: use_github_release() should use data in CRAN-RELEASE
description:
Currently `use_github_release()` just uses the HEAD commit for the tag, really it would be better to use the commit in `CRAN-RELEASE`, as that should be what was actually uploaded to CRAN.

This was mentioned in https://github.com/r-lib/devtools/issues/2139#issuecomment-546708187, but unfortunately no issue was ever opened in usethis.

title: `use_ragg()`
description:
Now that you can set ragg as your default graphics device in RStudio, I find myself recommending it to students because it's such a clear improvement to plot output, even on non-Windows machines. It would be nice to have something like `use_ragg()` that I can hand off to students much in the way I hand off `use_blank_slate()`.

Alternatively, there are also some options you can set in your R session: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/9275

Supporting specific RStudio preferences is a slippery slope, of course. I do feel that ragg is an unusually strong improvement to the default (similar to `use_blank_slate()`) that merits considering a specific function in usethis, but @ddsjoberg's [rstudio.prefs](https://github.com/ddsjoberg/rstudio.prefs) package also works well as a generalized solution to managing preferences programmatically.

title: use_options ?
description:
I find myself always going back to Hadley's book when I want to use options in packages, so I can copy paste and edit the below code:

```
.onLoad <- function(libname, pkgname) {
  op <- options()
  op.devtools <- list(
    devtools.path = "~/R-dev",
    devtools.install.args = "",
    devtools.name = "Your name goes here",
    devtools.desc.author = "First Last <first.last@example.com> [aut, cre]",
    devtools.desc.license = "What license is it under?",
    devtools.desc.suggests = NULL,
    devtools.desc = list()
  )
  toset <- !(names(op.devtools) %in% names(op))
  if(any(toset)) options(op.devtools[toset])
  
  invisible()
} 
```

A `use_options()` function might : 

* create a "zzz.R" file if there is none yet and no `.onLoad` function is defined anywhere
* write a `.onLoad`  function in "zzz.R" if none is defined anywhere
* have the body of `.onLoad` start with the code below if no usethis comments are found:

```
  ## usethis options: start
  op <- options()
  op.PKGNAME <- list(
   # edit and add options below
    PKGNAME.your_option = "your_default"
  )
  toset <- !(names(op.PKGNAME ) %in% names(op))
  if(any(toset)) options(op.PKGNAME[toset])
  ## usethis options: end ​
```

I'd use it often! Happy to contribute a PR  if it helps.

Thanks for the great work.

PS: Does it make sense to have `use_onload()` and `use_onattach` too to just create "zzz.R" and the empty function ?


I'm in VSCode where the `rstudioapi` is partially supported. So `rstudioapi::isAvailable()` returns `TRUE`. However this argument seems to be not so much about whether the API is available, but whether the user wishes to:

* Create an .Rproj file

Should the option should be renamed to something like: `use_project` which defaults to true if RStudio is detected?

How to detect RStudio is another question. Since the presence of the `rstudioapi` no longer guarantees the user is using RStudio. This should probably be raised as a separate issue over on `rstudioapi`.

title: Consistent Default for `copyright_holder` Parameter?
description:
I'm not certain this is either a bug report or a feature request, as this issue might simply reflect a deliberate choice by the authors to follow a legal convention of which I am unaware.

-----

Regarding the `copyright_holder` parameter, its (nonexistent) [default behavior](https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/blob/0d6522474e35c78391a0b54dc12d63a63a5ce05a/R/license.R#L141) in `use_proprietary_license()`
```
use_proprietary_license <- function(copyright_holder) {
  # ...
    copyright_holder = copyright_holder
  #...
}
```
seems inconsistent with its [default behavior](https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/blob/0d6522474e35c78391a0b54dc12d63a63a5ce05a/R/license.R#L60) in `use_mit_license()`
```
use_mit_license <- function(copyright_holder = NULL) {
  # ...
    copyright_holder = copyright_holder %||% glue("{project_name()} authors")
  #...
}
```
and (possibly) with its own [documentation](https://usethis.r-lib.org/reference/licenses.html#arguments):

> Name of the copyright holder or holders. This **defaults to "package name authors"**; you should only change this if you use a CLA to assign copyright to a single entity.

-----

As it stands, the call
```
use_proprietary_license()
```
throws the following error:
```
Error in use_proprietary_license() : 
  argument "copyright_holder" is missing, with no default
```
In contrast to the seamless call
```
use_mit_license()
```
the former seems a bit of a hiccup in the workflow.

# Question #

Should the convention ("package name authors") apply by default to a proprietary license

> Copyright 2021 `<package-name>` authors. All rights reserved.

just as it does to the MIT license?

> YEAR: 2021
> COPYRIGHT HOLDER: `<package-name>` authors

title: make usethis::use_*_license() friendly with github's license overview
description:
For example, running `usethis::use_mit_license()` creates both a LICENSE and a LICENSE.md file. Github seems to look to the LICENSE file to generate it's overview of the rights associated with the repo (therefore github thinks the repo is using an 'other' license type and doesn't give an overview of the LICENSE).

# Example

In [brshallo/pwiser](https://github.com/brshallo/pwiser) I have just a LICENSE file and github knows which license I'm using (MIT): 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/30487784/134727603-52f153c7-7589-4e57-b00e-3ddd8cdd10f4.png)

and shares a helpful overview of the rights when viewing the LICENSE
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/30487784/134727630-b58e4ae2-1304-48dd-a36a-79b2772a866b.png)

However in [brshallo/piececor](https://github.com/brshallo/piececor) I have both a LICENSE and LICENSE.md file and github does not know which license I am using (though again I'm using MIT):
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/30487784/134727670-2b5dbab3-b0b6-4327-9f2d-b3cac38cf05f.png)

And does not offer a helpful overview of rights when viewing either LICENSE or LICENSE.md:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/30487784/134727687-708c9dac-5bed-4b47-88d1-833b1d3a45ad.png)

Given that most new R packages are on github, it would be nice if `usethis::use_*_license()` produced file(s) in a way that made them friendly to github's rights overview. 

(Though could be better to open with github to suggest that their license overview identifies the file containing the actual license type...)

``` r
tmpdir <- withr::local_tempdir()
```

title: `~/.gitignore` is ignored
description:
I realize that I can't provide a reproducible example; I need to tell a story (sorry).

I recently upgraded my Mac to Big Sur. Of course, one of the first things I did was `install.packages("usethis")`, then `usethis::git_vaccinate()`.

I kept on seeing `.DS_Store` wanting to be committed, which was odd, so I kept adding it to local `.gitignore`. Finally, this morning, I said "enough" and started digging into it.

Of course, my `~/.gitignore` file looked OK, so a little investigation brought me to this [SO answer](https://stackoverflow.com/a/32487076), and sure enough, I did not have git's `core.excludesfile` set.

So I set `core.excludesfile`, and `.DS_Store` "went away".

I see that in [`edit_git_ignore()`](https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/blob/0d181f6905392b0c543a490d6047613334404bad/R/edit.R#L222-L227), if there is no global gitignore file: you set `core.excludesfile`, then call `git_vaccinate()`.

However, if you just call [`git_vaccinate()`](https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/blob/b3de0d7c18fdc1d0de0dc7616cbb85e823db9dac/R/git.R#L565-L568), I don't see that `core.excludesfile` gets set. I think this is how I got here.

As well [`git_vaccinated()`](https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/blob/b3de0d7c18fdc1d0de0dc7616cbb85e823db9dac/R/git.R#L570-L574) does not check that `core.excludesfile` is set.

I have a few ideas on some solutions, and will be happy to contribute, but I figure I'd let you react first.

Thanks!

title: A specific form of SSH URL is not parsed correctly
description:
Given a `.git/config` containing both HTTP and SSH git URLs, such as:

```ini
[remote "origin"]
	url = git@github.com:aronatkins/packrat.git
	fetch = +refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*
[remote "upstream"]
	url = https://github.com/rstudio/packrat
	fetch = +refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/upstream/*
```

Attempting to use `usethis::use_github_actions` errs:

```
> usethis::use_github_actions()
✓ Setting active project to '/Users/aron/dev/rstudio/packrat'
• Learn more at <https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/master/examples/README.md>
Error: Internal error: Multiple GitHub hosts
'github.com', 'git@github.com'
```

This problem can happen when the original clone happens when using one style of URL but adding an upstream URL using the other style of URL.

Workaround is to update the `.git/config` to use the same style of URL:

```ini
[remote "origin"]
	url = git@github.com:aronatkins/packrat.git
	fetch = +refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*
[remote "upstream"]
	url = git@github.com:rstudio/packrat.git
	fetch = +refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/upstream/*
```

title: `use_package("package", type = "Suggests")` does not demote package if already in imports
description:
Use case: If you forget to set the type to Suggests first time you use the function, or want to demote a package to Suggests to reduce installation dependencies.

Reproducible example: open a project containing a package and enter the following lines of code:

```r
usethis::use_package("bookdown")
usethis::use_package("bookdown", type = "Suggests")
```

That resulted in the following changes

```diff
-    sf
+    sf,
+    bookdown
 Suggests: 
     covr,
     curl,
```

It would be useful if `usethis` had the ability to move the package from Imports to Suggests, resulting in something like this:

```diff
@@ -26,7 +26,8 @@ Imports:
     boot,
     stplanr (>= 0.2.8),
     readr,
     sf
 Suggests: 
     covr,
-    curl
+   curl,
+   bookdown
```

title: Default edit_r_buildignore does not create an .Rbuildignore file in the project
`pandoc-citeproc` needed for bookdown rendering
description:
`pandoc-citeproc` is still needed to render references in bookdown (and possibly other places). However, `brew` no longer has `pandoc-citeproc` in the repo (https://formulae.brew.sh/formula/pandoc-citeproc).

The newer release of `usethis` reflects on the changes from `brew` by removing `pandoc-citeproc` from the installation steps (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/r-lib/actions/master/examples/bookdown.yaml), but the book will fail to build because bookdown will need to use citeproc to build.

These are the error messages from my own GH action builds:

Just making an update after 6 months
https://github.com/chendaniely/ds4biomed/runs/2376439679?check_suite_focus=true

```
Error: pandoc-citeproc has been disabled because it is deprecated upstream!
Error: Process completed with exit code 1.
```

Using updated `bookdown.yaml` file will pass the Install pandoc step, but will fail in the build site step
https://github.com/chendaniely/ds4biomed/runs/2376490402?check_suite_focus=true

```
Warning:  Deprecated: pandoc-citeproc filter. Use --citeproc instead.
Error running filter pandoc-citeproc:
Could not find executable pandoc-citeproc
Error: Error: pandoc document conversion failed with error 83
Execution halted
Error: Process completed with exit code 1.
```

Moved the `runs-on` from `mac-latest` to `ubuntu-latest- and add in `pandoc-citeproc` and `libcurl4-openssl-dev` along with some `renv` changes to get rid of the `rJava` dependency (`rJava` is not relevant to this issue)

https://github.com/chendaniely/ds4biomed/actions/runs/761956577

This is the `bookdown.yaml` file that worked for me

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
      - master

name: bookdown

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      GITHUB_PAT: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repo
        uses: actions/checkout@v2

      - name: Setup R
        uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@v1

      - name: Install pandoc pandoc-citeproc
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update -y
          sudo apt-get install -y pandoc pandoc-citeproc

      - name: Install system libraries
        run: |
          sudo apt-get install -y libcurl4-openssl-dev

      - name: Cache Renv packages
        uses: actions/cache@v2
        with:
          path: $HOME/.local/share/renv
          key: r-${{ hashFiles('renv.lock') }}
          restore-keys: r-

      - name: Cache bookdown results
        uses: actions/cache@v2
        with:
          path: _bookdown_files
          key: bookdown-${{ hashFiles('**/*Rmd') }}
          restore-keys: bookdown-

      - name: Install packages
        run: |
          R -e 'install.packages("renv")'
          R -e 'renv::restore()'

      - name: Build site
        run: Rscript -e 'bookdown::render_book("index.Rmd", quiet = TRUE, new_session = TRUE)'

      - name: Install npm
        uses: actions/setup-node@v1

      - name: Deploy to Netlify
        # NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN and NETLIFY_SITE_ID added in the repo's secrets
        env:
          NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN }}
          NETLIFY_SITE_ID: ${{ secrets.NETLIFY_SITE_ID }}
        run: |
          npm install netlify-cli -g
          netlify deploy --prod --dir _book
```

Is this a PR I should make into `r-lib`? for the yaml template? I'm not totally sure why `citeproc` was removed from `brew`, but is this potentially an issue in `bookdown`?
I also understand that the mac image was picked because it might make installing the R packages faster, so I'm not entirely sure what the correct "fix" would be?

Perhaps LazyData should only be set in the DESCRIPTION after calling `use_data()`, rather than being set in `create_package()`.

title: Feature request: browse_rseek()
description:
A common workflow I go through in R is to encounter an issue, open a browser window, search the issue on [rseek](https://rseek.org), then return to R. I love the speed that `usethis` brings with functions like `browse_github()`, and think `browse_rseek()` could be a great addition. While it moves further from the `browse_` family's focus on packages, I think it would be helpful for day-to-day R use.

I'd be happy to submit a pull request if this feature would be useful. This could also include `browse_google()`/`browse_duckduckgo()`/etc. if that would be beneficial.

title: Generalizing `use_tibble()` and `use_data_table()`
description:
`use_tibble()` and `use_data_table()` were marked as questioning in #1046 because:

> [they] don't do that much, and [they suggest] hundreds of other similar functions that might be added to usethis

Which is think is reasonable. I'm opening this issue to discuss if a generalized version of these functions is a good fit for usethis. I'm thinking something like `use_import(package, function = NULL)`. So, these functions would simply be replaced by these actions: `use_import("tibble", "tibble")` and `use_import("data.table")` or something to that effect. This generalization would primarily address the second reason above, but with respect to the first reason, I think usethis brings a consistency to roxygen imports that is very useful.

The reason I'm interested in this workflow is because, even though usethis is just adding a little roxygen, I like that it adds it to a consistent place and automates away that little bit of tedium, much like `use_package()`. Putting it in the package doc if it exists or using `ui_code_block()` otherwise is very nice to me. It has the added benefit of making such imports more consistent; they can be hard to find without digging around the docs or namespace, and if usethis has an opinion about where to put them, then I can start checking in one location to start.

title: Proposed feature: use_custom_build()
description:
I often repeat this pattern to get the Build All button for a custom build script and the Ctrl/Cmd+B shorcut linked to it:

1. create build script, like `build.R`, with the right shebang
2. open terminal, set permissions on build script
3. open project preferences to set custom build + point Rstudio to the script file

A  new `use_custom_build()` (or so) function would be useful. It could take a file name as input, then

1. if the file does not exist, create it from a template (shebang etc.) for common types (shell, R)
2. add execute permissions on Unix systems
3. set the `BuildType` and `CustomScriptPath` fields in *.Rproj, or stop and print a hint if there already is a BuildType field in *.Rproj

This could then be reused by more specialised workflow packages, which could wrap it with defaults set to their own build script templates, e.g. https://github.com/toddgrabowsky/tarflow/ (see https://github.com/toddgrabowsky/tarflow/issues/1)

A caveat is that shebangs may vary across systems and users, but this could be handled with a message prompting the user to review the script, or even opening it upon completion, adding a message or a comment in the file.

I'd be happy to do a PR if you think this fits into {usethis}. The only thing I am not sure about is what the most sensible way is to manipulate .Rproj files, as per https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/issues/1130#issuecomment-733927026.

title: GitHub PAT error with https protocol: detects user GH password instead of the token
description:
Hi,

Louise @lahuuki was setting up a new R package with `usethis` and we encountered a confusing error message that is really a `gh` error derived from `gitcreds` output.

```R
## Code
usethis::use_github()
```

```R
## Error + traceback
Error in validate_gh_pat(new_gh_pat(x)) : 
  A GitHub PAT must consist of 40 hexadecimal digits
> traceback()
10: stop(cond)
9: throw(new_error("A GitHub PAT must consist of 40 hexadecimal digits"))
8: validate_gh_pat(new_gh_pat(x))
7: gh_pat(token$password %||% "")
6: gh_token(.api_url)
5: .token %||% gh_token(.api_url)
4: gh::gh_whoami(.api_url = host)
3: withCallingHandlers(expr, message = function(c) if (inherits(c, 
       classes)) tryInvokeRestart("muffleMessage"))
2: suppressMessages(gh::gh_whoami(.api_url = host))
1: usethis::use_github()
```

This issue gets resolved if you run (or edit your `~/.Rprofile`) with:

```R
## For usethis::use_git()
options(usethis.protocol = "ssh")
```

which I had in my macOS but Louise didn't in her macOS setup.

Without those lines of code, Louise gets her GitHub password which is not 40 characters long.

```R
## Working through the internal code step by step in Louise's setup
> gh::gh_token(NULL)
Error in validate_gh_pat(new_gh_pat(x)) : 
  A GitHub PAT must consist of 40 hexadecimal digits
> gh:::default_api_url()
[1] "https://api.github.com"
> gh:::get_hosturl(gh:::default_api_url())
[1] "https://github.com"
> gitcreds::gitcreds_get(gh:::get_hosturl(gh:::default_api_url()))
<gitcreds>
  protocol: https
  host    : github.com
  username: lahuuki
  password: <-- hidden -->
> token <- gitcreds::gitcreds_get(gh:::get_hosturl(gh:::default_api_url()))
> token$password
```

while I indeed get my 40 characters long GitHub personal access token (PAT).

```R
## Working through the internal code step by step in my setup
> gh::gh_token(NULL)
(a truncated token, manually edited by me)
> gh:::default_api_url()
[1] "https://api.github.com"
> gh:::get_hosturl(gh:::default_api_url())
[1] "https://github.com"
> gitcreds::gitcreds_get(gh:::get_hosturl(gh:::default_api_url()))
<gitcreds>
  protocol: NA
  host    : NA
  username: NA
  password: <-- hidden -->
> token <- gitcreds::gitcreds_get(gh:::get_hosturl(gh:::default_api_url()))
> token$password
[1] "(I get a 40 character token here)"
> nchar(token$password)
[1] 40
```

The help file at https://usethis.r-lib.org/reference/git_protocol.html doesn't seem to indicate that using a `https` protocol would be a problem. Looking at our `~/.Rprofile` and `~/.gitconfig` nothing seems to jump at me. Both of us have a `GITHUB_PAT="40 characters long token"` entry in our `~/.Renviron`.

So, from the docs it seems to me that https is supported. I'm not sure if some specific configuration in Louise's setup is leading to the error, or if it's a change in the expected output from `gitcreds` inside the `gh` code. In any case, I'm reporting the issue here such that other `usethis` users can locate the error and solution more quickly that we did.

Best,
Leo

Session info:

```R
> packageVersion("gh")
[1] ‘1.2.0’
> packageVersion("gitcreds")
[1] ‘0.1.1’
> packageVersion("usethis")
[1] ‘2.0.0’
```

```
https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html)
```

title: travis yaml should include addons if usethis/gert is dependency
description: As this is a CI problem I can't provide a reprex, sorry. Currently the `use_travis()` function creates a yaml file with the following code ```yaml # R for travis: see documentation at https://docs.travis-ci.com/user/languages/r language: R cache: packages ``` The checks on Travis failed for my package because I have got `usethis` as a dependency which has `gert` as a dependency which requires libgit2 to be installed on the system (please see the following screenshot of the travis log). I found this solution https://github.com/r-lib/gert/issues/23#issuecomment-619511969 in the `gert` repo which is working fine for me. So I would suggest `use_travis()` creates the following yaml if `usethis` or `gert` are dependencies: ```yaml # R for travis: see documentation at https://docs.travis-ci.com/user/languages/r language: R cache: packages addons: apt: packages: - libgit2-dev ```

title: Latest usethis update doesn't compile with old versions of libgit2
description:
With old versions of `libgit2`, when compiling the `gert` package dependency, you are going to get a warning message telling you that your libgit2 version is too old, followed by a compilation error caused by a missing file (Sorry I didn't take note of the specific file before fixing the issue).

This is not exactly a bug but for anyone else trying to install `usethis` on systems whit no up to date versions of `libgit2` available, like in my case Raspbian Stretch only has `libgit2` 0.25.1 and you can't simply install a .deb package since it is an armhf architecture, you have to compile the package from source to get an update.

```
git clone https://github.com/libgit2/libgit2
cd libgit2
mkdir build && cd build
sudo su
cmake .. -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local
cmake --build . --target install
cd ..
rm -rf libgit2
exit
```
I'm aware this is not a proper bug report but I was told to post it here instead of replying to the publication on Community RStudio

New GitHub permissions may require 'workflow' scope for PAT
description:
GitHub ACL introduced a new `workflow` scope for PATs, which is required to push commits that change any files under `./github/workflows` in the repository. Hence, if you are using the API setup GHA, this scope is required.

It seems that GitHub has automatically enabled the `workflow` scope for existing PATs that already had the `repo` scope. So existing tokens are still good. However, for newly generated tokens, you may have to explicitly enable the  `workflow` scope.

title: FR: `browse_package()`
description:
I often find myself in the situation wanting to browse the pkgdown site of a package rather than its GitHub or CRAN site.

I am currently using `browseURL(desc::desc_get_urls()[1])` for this which opens the pkgdown site if it exists in the URL field and comes first. If missing, the GitHub page is opened. If no URL field exists, it errors obviously.

Some pkgs do not have a URL field at all and while `usethis::browse_github()` already falls back to `usethis::browse_cran()`, I have the feeling that a wrapper function like `browse_package()` could be helpful.

Essentially it would try to look for a pkgdown page first, fall back to the GitHub page and last to the CRAN page.

Feature request: allow to add licenses to non-package projects
description:
When setting up a (non-package) project, I repeatedly have to google for well formatted plain text versions of software licenses. It would be great if the `use_xx_license()` functions would not be limited to package projects, but allow to skip the [`check_is_package(..)` step](https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/blob/master/R/license.R#L42).

Current:

```r
> setwd(tempdir())
> usethis::use_mit_license(name = "Test")
Error: Path '/tmp/Rtmp7uX3Yq/' does not appear to be inside a project or package.
In addition: Warning message:
In path_file(base_path) : restarting interrupted promise evaluation
```

Desired:

```r
> setwd(tempdir())
> usethis::use_lgpl_license(name = "Test", check_project = FALSE)
File LICENSE.md created.
```

Alternatively, exposing the `use_license_template()` function and a list of allowed names, or some clever regexing on the names, could also be an option. However, this would prohibit special cases, such as the year-copyright file for MIT.

```r
# some ideas
usethis::list_templates(type = "license")
usethis::list_license_templates()

# with some magic
usethis::use_license_template("Apache")
```

title: Automatic replacing of the lifecycle badge
description:
The `use_lifecycle_badge()` is intended to report the state of the package and it can change more often than other badges (thinking now on the move from travis to github actions...) .

Recently I have archived an experimental package and to my surprise the new badge was added instead of replacing the existing lifecycle badge. 

It would be nice if there was an option to override an existing badge with the new lifecycle stage. The default could be TRUE and if not found any badge to replace then add it.
 
This would mean finding if there is an old badge and then placing the new badge there. Perhaps it could be easily done with a couple of regex as much of the links (both for the image and to the stage) would be the same.

title: Leverage renv to use_all_packages in usethis: bad idea?, makes sense?
description:
Would it make sense to have a `use_all_packages` function to automate a step further adding package dependencies to DESCRIPTION?

This is (sort of) a feature request, but mainly a question: do you guys think this is a good/bad idea?, or if it makes sense at all.

What I have in mind is something like this: to use {renv} to find all `dependencies()` in your package and automatically add them  to DESCRIPTION (using `usethis::use_package`). So something like this would do:

```r
use_all_packages <- function() {
  undesc_deps <- renv::dependencies() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(fromdesc = endsWith(Source, "/DESCRIPTION")) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(Package) %>%
    dplyr::summarize(indesc = any(fromdesc)) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!indesc) %>%
    dplyr::filter(Package != usethis::proj_get() %>% basename()) %>%
    dplyr::filter(Package != "renv") %>%
    dplyr::filter(Package != "purrr")

  purrr::walk(undesc_deps$Package, usethis::use_package)  
}
```
(of course it would need to be much better implemented to make it into usethis; this is just a quick-and-dirty snippet that gets the job done).

Would love to hear your thoughts about this.

title: Add option in use_zip not to automatically open file manager after download
description:
This is my first time suggesting a feature for a package and using a reprex, so I'm not sure if I am following protocol. Apologies beforehand. 

If one would want to download a series of zips automatically, it could be a nuisance to see them opening in the file manager one after another. 

```r
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(usethis)
library(rvest)

url_zips <- "https://www.gob.mx/salud/documentos/datos-abiertos-bases-historicas-direccion-general-de-epidemiologia"

read_html(url_zips) %>% 
  html_nodes(".bottom-buffer a") %>% 
  tail(3) %>% 
  walk(~ html_attr(.x,"href") %>% 
         use_zip(destdir = here(), cleanup = TRUE))
```

I think there could be an extra parameter for use_zip, and the underlying tidy_unzip, to allow the user not to see the file manager after the download:

```r
# pass new parameter to tidy_unzip
use_zip <- function (url, destdir = getwd(), cleanup = if (rlang::is_interactive()) NA else FALSE, open_file_manager = TRUE) 
{
  url <- normalize_url(url)
  check_path_is_directory(destdir)
  ui_done("Downloading from {ui_value(url)}")
  zipfile <- tidy_download(url, destdir)
  ui_done("Download stored in {ui_path(zipfile)}")
  check_is_zip(attr(zipfile, "content-type"))
  tidy_unzip(zipfile, cleanup, open_file_manager) 
}

# using the new parameter in the last else if
tidy_unzip <- function (zipfile, cleanup = FALSE,open_file_manager=TRUE) 
{
  base_path <- path_dir(zipfile)
  filenames <- utils::unzip(zipfile, list = TRUE)[["Name"]]
  filenames <- filenames[filenames != "/"]
  filenames <- filenames[keep_lgl(filenames)]
  td <- top_directory(filenames)
  loose_parts <- is.na(td)
  if (loose_parts) {
    target <- path_ext_remove(zipfile)
    utils::unzip(zipfile, files = filenames, exdir = target)
  }
  else {
    target <- path(path_dir(zipfile), td)
    utils::unzip(zipfile, files = filenames, exdir = path_dir(zipfile))
  }
  ui_done("Unpacking ZIP file into {ui_path(target, base_path)} \\\n    ({length(filenames)} files extracted)")
  if (isNA(cleanup)) {
    cleanup <- is_interactive() && ui_yeah("Shall we delete the ZIP file ({ui_path(zipfile, base_path)})?")
  }
  if (isTRUE(cleanup)) {
    ui_done("Deleting {ui_path(zipfile, base_path)}")
    file_delete(zipfile)
  }
  if (is_interactive()) {
    rproj_path <- dir_ls(target, regexp = "[.]Rproj$")
    if (length(rproj_path) == 1 && rstudioapi::hasFun("openProject")) {
      ui_done("Opening project in RStudio")
      rstudioapi::openProject(target, newSession = TRUE)
    }
    else if ((!in_rstudio_server()) & open_file_manager) {
      ui_done("Opening {ui_path(target, base_path)} in the file manager")
      utils::browseURL(path_real(target))
    }
  }
  invisible(target)
}

```

````
title: Minor suggestion for use_spell_check()
description:
Hey y'all!

I've just used `use_spell_check()` for the first time and i messed up and didn't change `lang` arg. So i runned it again with `use_spell_check(lang = "pt-BR)` (it's a private package for automating a process in my office, so it's in native language) but then i've got:
```
Erro: Language has a different value in DESCRIPTION.Use `overwrite = TRUE` to overwrite.
```
So i had to run the unexported (or typing manually) `usethis:::use_description_field("Language", "pt-BR", overwrite = TRUE)` and then run again `use_spell_check(lang = "pt-BR)`.

So i suggest setting `overwrite = TRUE` (see below) in `use_spell_check()`.

```
use_spell_check <- function(vignettes = TRUE, lang = "en-US", error = FALSE) {
  check_is_package("use_spell_check")
  check_installed("spelling")
  use_dependency("spelling", "Suggests")
  use_description_field("Language", lang, overwrite = TRUE) ######################## look here!
  spelling::spell_check_setup(
    pkg = proj_get(), vignettes = vignettes, lang = lang, error = error
  )
  ui_todo("Run {ui_code('devtools::check()')} to trigger spell check")
}
```

title: Reveal GitHub PAT's scopes in git_sitrep()
description:
The group test drive revealed two surprises that were due to unexpected scopes:

* Some people couldn't see the emails associated with their GitHub accounts. That's because their PAT did not have the `"user:email"` scope. That is now included in the default scopes set for `create_github_token()`, but that was not always the case.
* One person had a PAT with **no** scopes. So that broke lots of things and, upon discussion, affected other packages as well, such as remotes.

In both cases, seeing explicit scopes would probably have helped us troubleshoot more quickly.

title: Default to "main" in github actions
description:
Brief description of the problem

This issue is inspired by my own experience using usethis' github actions in [newsanchor](https://github.com/CorrelAid/newsanchor) and [pocketapi](https://github.com/CorrelAid/pocketapi) and [this tweet](https://twitter.com/coolbutuseless/status/1314465384276389888?s=20) by @coolbutuseless. 

New GitHub repos are now using `main` as default branch by default, see [here](https://github.com/github/renaming) unless a different default branch is set in user / organization settings. Hence, more and more repositories will have main as default branch. For those repos, the github actions provided via `usethis` do not work out of the box and have to be adapted (for example, see [this commit](https://github.com/CorrelAid/newsanchor/commit/cab71fea43d769071714b8edf924a95705df954a)). 

I understand that there is a trade-off between supporting existing repositories still running on `master` with default branch. However, given that the R community is not afraid to adapt / move forward and that in the future, a lot more `main` repos will be there because of GitHub's new defaults, I think there is definitely a case to change the defaults in `usethis` GitHub actions as well. :)

title: idea for GHE extension-mechanism
description:
This is reposted, and lightly edited, from #836.

The goal is to provide an extension mechanism for GitHub Enterprise (GHE).

There are a few r-lib packages (usethis, remotes, and pak come to mind; there may be others) that rely on or interact with git and github. I think that this idea could be used by other packages, should they wish.

I wonder if there could be a list of "r-lib" github options, like follows:

```r
rlib.github.default <- 
  list(
    service = "github",
    name = "GitHub"
    host_git = "github.com",
    url_api = "https://api.github.com",
    url_web = "https://github.com",
    env_token = c("GITHUB_PAT", "GITHUB_TOKEN")
  )
```

I have "renamed" some of the elements to try to identify more clearly what each element does; I note that the definition of `host` can vary from function to function (e.g. `remotes::install_github()`, `usethis::create_from_github()`, `usethis::browse_github_pat()`).

Perhaps this option could be a hardwired default, so that if someone wanted to use an instance of GitHub Enterprise (GHE), they could add something like this to their `.Rprofile`:

```r
options(
  rlib.github = list(
    list(
      service = "ghe_acme",
      name = "Acme GitHub Enterprise"
      host_git = "github.acme.com",
      url_api = "https://github.acme.com/api/v3",
      url_web = "https://github.acme.com",
      env_token = "GITHUB_PAT_ACME"
    )
  )
)
```

The overall idea is that public-facing functions that touch github (public or GHE) could add a `service` argument that could be used to determine the rest of the information. For organizations that use GHE, it would be their responsibility to publicize internally the "thing" that folks would put in their `.Rprofile`.

I think of functions in four categories:

- creating at github: `usethis::use_github()`
- creating from github: `usethis::create_from_github()`, `remotes::install_github()`
- interacting with github: `usethis::pr_*()`
- utilities: `usethis::github_token()`, `usethis::browse_github_token()`, `usethis::git_sitrep()`

For creating at github, I might suggest a default of `service = NULL`. If there is only one service available (github), it would use it. If there are multiple services available, and none is specified, the user could be told to supply an explicit choice.

For creating from github, I perhaps `service = "github"` could work as a default. I could also see wanting to be explicit.

For interacting with github, the `pr_*` functions, I don't think a `service` argument would be appropriate. Instead, I think these functions could look at the git-remote address for `origin` or `upstream`, e.g. `git@github.com:r-lib/usethis.git`, pull out `host_git`, then use the matching service.

For the utility functions, I think `service = "github"` would work OK as a default. For `usethis::git_sitrep()`, perhaps it could report on the status of all registered services, and let the user know which of the services is being used for a local repo.

title: Owner/repo and owner/repo produce different git_sitrep()
description:
Usually, the letter case of the repo specification is unimportant:
ThisOwner/repo is equivalent to thisowner/repo.

I expected to get the same result with an upstrem set to either of these two urls: 
1. "git@github.com:2DegreesInvesting/r2dii.data.git"
2. "git@github.com:2degreesinvesting/r2dii.data.git"

However, those two urls produce different `git_sitrep()` output; the problem is that (2) fails to configure support for PRs as indicated by the message __"The 'origin' GitHub remote is a fork, but its parent is not configured as the 'upstream' remote."__

``` r
library(usethis)
packageVersion("usethis")
#> [1] '1.6.1.9001'

# This works as expected
use_git_remote(
  "upstream",
  "git@github.com:2DegreesInvesting/r2dii.data.git",
  overwrite = TRUE
)
#> ✓ Setting active project to '/home/mauro/git/r2dii.data'
usethis:::github_remote_config()
#> type = 'fork'
#> Config supports a pull request = TRUE
#> origin = 'maurolepore/r2dii.data' (can push) = fork of '2DegreesInvesting/r2dii.data'
#> upstream = '2DegreesInvesting/r2dii.data' (can push)
#> desc = 'origin' is a fork of '2DegreesInvesting/r2dii.data', which is configured as the 'upstream' remote.
camel <- git_sitrep()
#> Git config (global)
#> * Name: 'Mauro Lepore'
#> * Email: 'maurolepore@gmail.com'
#> * Vaccinated: TRUE
#> usethis + gert
#> * Default usethis protocol: <unset>
#> * gert supports HTTPS: FALSE
#> * gert supports SSH: TRUE
#> GitHub
#> * Personal access token: '<found in env var>'
#> * User: 'maurolepore'
#> * Name: 'Mauro Lepore'
#> * Email(s): '<unknown>'
#> Repo
#> * Path: '/home/mauro/git/r2dii.data'

#> desc = 'origin' is a fork of '2DegreesInvesting/r2dii.data', which is configured as the 'upstream' remote.



# This fails because the letter case is different between the repo specification
# on GitHub and the upstream url on my local repo (compare ThisOwner/repo vs. 
# thisowner/repo).
use_git_remote(
  "upstream",
  "git@github.com:2degreesinvesting/r2dii.data.git",
  overwrite = TRUE
)
usethis:::github_remote_config()
#> type = 'fork_upstream_is_not_origin_parent'

title: GPL license tweaks
description:
GPLv2 or greater is a little friendlier than GPLv3 or greater since it's clearly directly compatible with R's license. We should provide this as a default, possibly deprecating `use_gpl3_license()` (maybe with new `version` argument).

In either case, we should default to using "or greater" as otherwise packages that use GPL v2 are not automatically compatible with GPLv3. See (e.g) https://opensource.stackexchange.com/questions/1777/why-is-gplv2-incompatible-with-gplv3

title: use_gpl3_license() modifies GPL-3 license text
description: Calling `usethis::use_gpl3_license("My name")` produces a modified `LICENSE.md` file, with "modified" denoting modifications compared to the [original license text](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0.md). In particular, the name of the R package and the text passed to `usethis::use_gpl3_license()`'s argument `name` (`"My name"` in the example above) are used in section "How to Apply These Terms to Your New Programs" of the license text. However, it seems like modifying the GPL-3 license text is not allowed (not even for section "How to Apply These Terms to Your New Programs"), see for example [here](https://softwareengineering.stackexchange.com/questions/281949/how-to-properly-apply-a-license). I'm not an expert for legal affairs (and I also don't know if the person who answered in that Stack Exchange thread is one), but it makes sense to me that this section "How to Apply These Terms to Your New Programs" is intentioned to be a template and therefore must be included unmodified.

title: Tutorials created with use_tutorial can't be found by learnr::run_tutorial
description:
I'm currently working on a "tutorial package" for tidymodels called [learntidymodels](https://github.com/tidymodels/learntidymodels). 
We expect users to install this package and open their tutorial of choice locally by using `learnr::run_tutorial()` function.

When I use `usethis::use_tutorial` to add tutorials to the package, it adds the newly created tutorial `.Rmd` to `.Rbuildignore`. Consequently, `learnr::run_tutorial()` or `learnr::available_tutorials()` functions can't find the tutorial(s) and throw an error. 

For example:
```
library(usethis)
path <- file.path(tempdir(), "mypkg")
create_package(path)
use_tutorial("tutorial", "Some tutorial")
devtools::install()

learnr::run_tutorial("tutorial", "mypkg")
#> Error: No tutorials found for package: "mypkg"
```

I am not sure if there's a specific reason why these tutorial Rmds should be included in `.Rbuildignore`. 
But when these `.Rmd` files **are not** added to `.Rbuildignore` everything works fine and package still seems to pass all R CMD checks. On the other hand `use_tutoria()` adds the rendered html files to `.gitignore` and it may make sense to add these to `.Rbuildignore` as well?

https://github.com/ThinkR-open/golem/tree/master/inst/shinyexample/dev

The idea behind these scripts is that anyone starting a new Shiny App with `{golem}` can follow a series of common steps. Newcomers are then guided, and seasoned developers are sure they don't forget anything. 

To some extent, I think this can be applied to a lot of cases, and in particular to package development, which (almost always) contains the same steps, more or less the one from https://github.com/ThinkR-open/golem/blob/master/inst/shinyexample/dev/01_start.R: 

- filling DESCRIPTION 
- creating README
- use licence
- use news
etc. 

Same goes before building: one will test locally, check for CRAN with r-hub, etc.

Maybe a `usethis::use_dev_script()` would be nice, with a series of steps to follow when creating a package?

title: Feature request: extend use_dev_package() beyond github.com
description:
As far as I can tell, right now, `use_dev_package()` assumes that the remote is located at github.com, and it constructs a Remotes entry based on that assumption, e.g. `r-lib/usethis`.

To extend to other situations, could `use_dev_package()` be an additional argument, `remote` with a default of `NULL`? Of course, the default behavior would be the current behavior. A non-NULL `remote` provided to the function could become the entry in Remotes.

I would not think this useful for direct interactive use; my use case is to write a wrapper function for institutional use, for example:

```r
use_package_acme <- function(package) {

  remote <- get_acme_remote(package) # Acme's responsibility

  usethis::use_dev_package(package, remote = remote)
}
```

use_r(template = TRUE)

Should result in something like

#' Title

#'

}

title: [Feature request] Automate configuration of Rtools40 on Windows
description:
Could **usethis** automate the configuration of RTools40 on Windows (described on https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/)? The function should check if `"~/.Renviron"` file exists, if yes, should check if a line with the following code is present:

```r
PATH="${RTOOLS40_HOME}\usr\bin;${PATH}"
```

If the file is missing or the line of code is missing, the line should be added **without removing** any content that is already present in `"~/.Renviron"`  file.

title: use_github_action("pkgdown") fails without error message
description:
I aimed to add a github.io-website to my package by using the following code and pushed the changes to a feature branch on github (generated `.yaml`-file and changes in `.Rbuildignore`, [this commit](https://github.com/inbo/forrescalc/commit/6ae28b26faa81f91f57468c6984980748c6ecc9d))
```r
usethis::use_pkgdown()
usethis::use_github_action("pkgdown")
```
When merging the changes to the master branch, the run failed without showing an error: [the report](https://github.com/inbo/forrescalc/runs/798313752) only mentions successful installations.

I tried adding a branch `gh-pages` with only one empty file index.html (as it seemed not possible to push an empty branch) because I was not sure if it should be added manually, but the run [failed again](https://github.com/inbo/forrescalc/runs/799430785) with exactly the same report.

Nevertheless, a while ago the same procedure worked fine when applying it to another package.  I was then pleasantly surprised that the setup went so easy and fast.

title: Creating License files when filling from usethis.description option
description:
I've stored in my .Rprofile an option for `usethis.description`:

```r
usethis.description = list(...,
		License = "MIT + file LICENSE",
        ...)
```
When I created a new package (via rstudio new project R package from devtools) I saw the description included it. However, I didn't see it populated with the LICENSE and LICENSE.md files I would get if I used `use_mit_license()`. 

Maybe it can be added that if there is an option of `usethis.description$License`, to run the appropriate `use_*_license()` (if possible) to create those files. It will make it easier to not forget them. 

Probably related to #159 but I don't have set up options for devtools, only for blogdown and Ncpus.

description: Getting travis to deploy pkgdown pages as part of the CI is not straightforward and should be better documented...

title: Show warning only once
description: Using usethis::use_warn in functions will show warning every time the function is called. It would be beneficiary to have an argument for only showing the warning once/first time.

title: Check licenses restrictions/compatibility on use_package
description:
Some licenses have more restrictions than others, so they might end up blocking some uses. If a package with a more restrictive license is used by another package and is distributed there is a potential point of conflict (specially in commercial settings). Perhaps this could be checked on `use_package`?

I think it would help users if we got (at least) a warning if the licenses are incompatible and nothing if they are ok. This could be restricted to approved licenses as it is now and if there is a custom license a message should appear to make the user check if the license are compatible. 

This image ([from FOS](https://opensource.stackexchange.com/a/3)) can be helpful to determine if the code is compatible, together with the section [4.1.2 Dependencies in DESCRIPTION](https://thinkr-open.github.io/licensing-r/rlicense.html#4.12) of Licensing R from Colin Fay:
![](https://i.stack.imgur.com/k1G9Z.jpg)

title: Link to roxygen2 vignette (markdown) is broken in CONTRIBUTING.md
description:
After the PR in dplyr (https://github.com/tidyverse/dplyr/pull/5166) I checked the CONTRIBUTING.md file in tibble. I saw that the link to the roxygen2 vignette is broken there, too. This broken link is scattered over some more tidyverse and r-lib packages:
``` r
library(gh)
library(httr)
library(dplyr)
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'dplyr'
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:stats':
#> 
#>     filter, lag
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:base':
#> 
#>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union

check_one_pkg <- function(pkg_name, username) {
  contributing_url <- paste0("https://github.com/", username, "/", pkg_name, 
                             "/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md")
  contributing_file <- GET(contributing_url)
  status_code <- status_code(contributing_file)
  if (status_code != 200) {
    wrong_url <- FALSE
  } else {
    contributing_file <- content(contributing_file, "text")
    wrong_url <- grepl("https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/roxygen2/vignettes/markdown.html", 
                       contributing_file, fixed = TRUE)
  }
  data.frame(pkg_name = pkg_name, contributing_url = contributing_url,
             status_code = status_code, wrong_url = wrong_url)
}

check_pkgs <- function(username, .limit) {
  pgk_names <- gh("GET /users/:username/repos", username = username, .limit =  .limit)
  pgk_names <- vapply(pgk_names, "[[", "", "name")
  check_res <- lapply(pgk_names, check_one_pkg, username = username)
  check_res <- do.call(rbind, check_res)
  check_res
}

tidyverse_res <- check_pkgs("tidyverse", 35)
all(tidyverse_res$status_code %in% c(200, 404)) # 404: file does not exist
#> [1] TRUE
tidyverse_res %>% filter(wrong_url) %>% select(pkg_name)
#>         pkg_name

title: Bioc-friendly feature suggestions
description:
Hi,

Based on my recent work for https://github.com/r-lib/actions/issues/84 and at https://github.com/leekgroup/derfinderPlot/blob/master/dev/01_setup.R, I want to make a few small PRs to `usethis`.

## PR idea 1

One of them is basically about mentioning the Bioconductor Support website for `.github/SUPPORT.md`. Currently I did so at https://github.com/leekgroup/derfinderPlot/blob/master/dev/01_setup.R#L36-L45 but it could be it's own function or editing the tidyverse template (which you might not want to do as it would be a more global change).

```
## Customize the support message to mention the Bioconductor Support Website
usethis::use_tidy_support()
support <- readLines(".github/SUPPORT.md")
support <-
    gsub(
        "\\[community.rstudio.com\\]\\(https://community.rstudio.com/\\), and/or StackOverflow",
        "the [Bioconductor Support Website](https://support.bioconductor.org/) using the appropriate package tag",
        support
    )
writeLines(support, ".github/SUPPORT.md")
```

## PR idea 2

A second one could be a badge that has a specific message for the GitHub action I'm suggesting at https://github.com/r-lib/actions/issues/84 .

## PR idea 3

I also have a more custom `issue_template.md` https://github.com/leekgroup/derfinderPlot/blob/master/dev/01_setup.R#L47-L51. Since that code uses `:::` at some point, maybe a function that allows custom templates would be useful.

Before making any PRs, I wanted to bring these ideas up.

Best,
Leo

title: use_namespace(roxygen=FALSE) creates an invalid NAMESPACE
description:
```{r}
usethis::create_package("foo", roxygen = FALSE)
devtools::install()
```
fails with
```
** building package indices
Error : '\.' is an unrecognized escape in character string starting ""^[^\."
ERROR: installing namespace metadata failed
```
because https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/blob/582a3fa886c042fe6c91376a6e4332df09a3db2a/R/namespace.R#L19 creates a namespace with text

```
$ cat NAMESPACE
exportPattern("^[^\.]")
```
 The escaped `.` needs to be `\\\\.`

title: `use_data(..., internal = TRUE)` should consider an `add` option
description:
Internal data are all stored in a single file `R/sysdata.rda`. For packages developed over time or which includes many datasets, it could be useful to include an option `add` to `use_data()` that can be activated (and have effect only) when `internal = TRUE`.

That would permit developers of the package to add internal data to the package as the package grown, without the needs to rerun all the setup scripts and without the need to include all of their code in single script with a single call of `use_data(..., internal = TRUE)` at its end.

```r
# 20200304-internal.R
# internal data that can be processed on 2020-03-04 only

20200304_data <- mtcars

usethis::use_data(20200304_data,
  internal = TRUE
)
```

```r
# 20200404-internal.R
# internal data that can be processed on 2020-04-04 only
# (without possibility to re-run 20200304-internal.R)
# (saving this code on its own file)

20200404_data <- iris

usethis::use_data(20200404_data ,
  internal = TRUE,
  add = TRUE
)
```

title: Work draft PRs into the pr_*() flow
description:
Workflow described by @DavisVaughan:

- `pr_init()`
- Do some commits, get it working locally
- `pr_push()` and open a draft pr. This lets you see CI but doesnt notify anyone
- Continue work and routinely `pr_push()` to trigger CI
- Switch from draft pr to real pr *Jenny: maybe we facilitate this? also easy to do in browser*
- Now get a review from collaborators and merge
- `pr_finish()`

Context: he's not a big user of `pr_init()` and part of the reason is he wants to work on the branch more quietly until he's ready for review. So making an early WIP PR is not attractive, which `pr_push()` pushes you towards, but maybe draft PR is a good compromise.

title: Fix use_pkgdown_travis() issues related to Tracis-CI dpl v2
description:
It seems that Tracis-CI went to dpl v2 lately. This causes issues in deploying **pkgdown** websites with  `usethis::use_pkgdown_travis()`. E.g., dpl v2 does not use the argument `skip_cleanup` anymore (see [here](https://github.com/travis-ci/dpl#cleaning-up-the-git-working-directory) and warning in figure below), but `use_pkgdown_travis()` still sets this parameter:

https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/blob/b2e894eb6d1d7f3312a783db3bb03a7cc309ba61/R/pkgdown.R#L69

This is a print screen of Travis-CI warnings and messages on settings in `.travis.yml` file:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12725868/78533062-f6852a00-77f0-11ea-9383-19ef3dde1b8f.png)

So as I understand, the deployment code in `.tavis.yml` should look something like this:
```yaml
before_cache: Rscript -e 'remotes::install_cran("pkgdown")'
deploy:
  provider: script
  script: Rscript -e 'pkgdown::deploy_site_github()'
```

There are other messages that suggest explicitly stating what OS and its distribution should be used and writing the language (i.e., `r`) in lower case but I'm not sure if these are related to **usethis**: 
```yaml
language: r
cache: packages
os: linux
dist: xenial
```

title: use_testthat() fails for Shiny apps
description:
In the next version of Shiny we're planning on releasing a new function for running tests in the application environment, `shiny::runTests()` https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/pull/2585

This will promote the use of `testthat` in Shiny apps.

I thought to start a discussion here on `usethis::use_testthat()`'s behavior with respect to this change. Currently, running it in a Shiny app results in the following error message:
```
Error: `use_testthat()` is designed to work with packages.
```
We hope to promote unit testing in Shiny apps moving forward, and I thought it might be good for `use_testthat()` to work in this case.

Unfortunately, Shiny doesn't have a predicate function to determine whether or not the current directory is plausibly a Shiny app. However, I think the logic's pretty simple: at a minimum, there has to be either an `app.R` or both a `server.R` and `ui.R` in the current directory.

So, one way forward would be to check for package *and* Shiny app plausibility, and bail otherwise, but as a non-expert on all things `usethis` I'm looking forward to hearing how other people think it should work.

Thanks in advance for your feedback, and consider me on the hook for whatever implementation is needed 👍

title: use_github_release() fails uninformatively when there are no lines in NEWS.md section
description:
Brief description of the problem

When no lines exist in the latest section of NEWS.md, `use_github_release()` returns `Error in text[[1]] : subscript out of bounds`.

Reprex:

NEWS.md:
```
# pkg 0.2.0

# pkg 0.1.0

* news line
```

Code run:
```r
use_github_release
```

The error occurs in [`news_latest()`](https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/blob/23c9119afa49a7e6fd153aa204219f065a9f0ea1/R/release.R#L172) where code removing blank lines errors on an empty string.

This probably typically occurs because the user has taken `usethis` steps out of sequence, so the most sensible solution would be to stop with an informative error and advise the user to document the release in NEWS.md. Alternatively the function could pass the resulting newline and issue a warning advising the user to document their release when submitting the form on Github.

Happy to try a PR if you can indicate which solution you prefer.

title: `use_dev_package` should handle more remote types
description:
`use_dev_package` can only handle dev packages installed from github remotes. 

A simple change to the `package_remote` function would make `use_dev_package` work with any remote type that has a `Remotes` field of the form `{RemoteType}::{RemoteUsername}/{RemoteRepo}`.

In particular, this would cover package dependencies from `GitLab` and `Bitbucket`.

Something like this:

```R
package_remote <- function(package) {
  desc <- desc::desc(package = package)
  remote_info <- desc$get(c("RemoteType", "RemoteUsername", "RemoteRepo"))
  
  supported_remotes <- c("github", "gitlab", "bitbucket")
  is_valid_remote <- 
    rlang::is_string(remote_info[["RemoteType"]]) && 
    remote_info[["RemoteType"]] %in% supported_remotes
  
  if (!is_valid_remote) {
    ui_stop("{ui_value(package)} was not installed from a supported remote type.")
  }
  
  glue::glue_data(as.list(remote_info), "{RemoteType}::{RemoteUsername}/{RemoteRepo}")
}
```

I don't really see a reason to restrict the remotes to github, gitlab and bitbucket though. I would just check that `RemoteType`, `RemoteUsername` and `RemoteRepo` are not `NA`.

The code above would add an explicit `github::` prefix to github remotes but this could obviously be avoided. IMO `usethis` is github-centric enough as it is, so I would leave the prefix for clarity.

This is related to #293 to the extent that it is about extending the functionalities beyond github, but this is a simpler (and probably more common) use case.

I started a new package following the Rstudio new project > R package >  git then I used some of the `usethis` functions to set up the package.

The history of command run is: 
```r
use_rstudio()
use_git()
use_mit_license()
use_testthat()
use_package("package")
desc::desc_normalize()
use_readme_rmd()
use_travis() # Error shown below
use_github()
use_coverage()
use_vignette("name")
?use_github
git_sitrep() # Sitrep shown below

title: FR: use_lintr function to help set up code linting for package
description:
The package does not have a `use_lintr` helper, but I use the `lintr` package with all of my packages and it is helpful to have a function that can automate the set up of this piece of package scaffolding. Others may find it similarly useful.

I see three typical ways to use `lintr` with a package:
 
* local interactive use
* automatic use on Travis CI post-build (non-failing)
* automatic local and Travis CI as a unit test (failing)

I think the first option should be the default. It is the simplest. The second option is the official recommended approach, which involves adding to .travis.yml:

```
after_success:
  - R CMD INSTALL $PKG_TARBALL
  - Rscript -e 'lintr::lint_package()'
```

but this option is specifically for cases where someone does not wish to have a unit test, or a build failure when the linter finds style issues.

The third option is the most rigorous and is intended to fail a build, locally and on Travis, if there are style issues present. Personally, I use this option almost exclusively in my packages, but it should not be the default because it is the most complex and also may not be desirable for long-running test suites.

I have an initial version of a function and will submit a pull request.

title: Should `use_package()` remove details set by `use_dev_package()`?
description:
`use_dev_package()` sets a minimum version number and the location of the remote repository. 

E.g., a dev version of ggplot2 produces

```r
# remotes::install_github("tidyverse/ggplot2")
use_dev_package("ggplot2")
```

```yaml
Imports: 
    ggplot2 (>= 3.2.1.9000)
Remotes:  
    tidyverse/ggplot2
```

To me, `use_package()`, by virtue of its contrast with `use_dev_package()`, implies a CRAN package. But if I use `use_package()` after, nothing changes.

```r
# install.packages("ggplot2")
use_package("ggplot2")
```

```yaml
Imports: 
    ggplot2 (>= 3.2.1.9000)
Remotes:  
    tidyverse/ggplot2
```

And using a new min version (as you might after a new CRAN release that has features you depended on from the dev version) only changes that part, assuming the new version is higher than the dev version. It does not modify `Remotes`.

```r
use_package("ggplot2", min_version = TRUE)
```

```yaml
Imports: 
    ggplot2 (>= 3.3.0)
Remotes:  
    tidyverse/ggplot2
```

In principle, this code still works, but it seems like `use_package()` should investigate this more. e.g., if there is an existing dev package, ask `ui_yeah()` if you want to a) upgrade the min version and b) remove remotes. I had expected it to change something, but it didn't. It also seems that to be a reasonable default workflow after depending on a remote dev package.

title: Don't install README pre-commit hook if R package precommit is installed by default
description:
`usethis::use_readme_rmd()` initialises a bare git pre-commit hook (i.e. write a simple script to .git/hooks/pre-commit) when git is used. However, users who use the pre-commit framework (e.g. via https://github.com/lorenzwalthert/precommit) at the same time may not want this hook to be initlized because they want to use the pre-commit framework exclusively for managing hooks to avoid friction.

Hence, I propose that `usethis::use_readme_rmd()` exposes an argument `add_git_hook` defaulting to `!rlang::is_installed("precommit")`. This way, the hook only get's initiated if {precommit} is not installed. The assumption here is that people who create a new README and have precommit installed most likely want to use equivalent of usethis' precommit hook from the {precommit} package. If that's not the case, the can still override the default argument and set `add_git_hook` to `TRUE`.  

This proposal alleviates problems mentioned in your [previous statement ](https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/issues/849#issuecomment-514266345) that the existing hook is already a source of complaint and friction and hook management is generally out of the scope of {usethis}. Would you be open to review a PR that implements this?

title: `pr_finish()`: Delete local branch if remote was deleted
description:
When the remote has been deleted and I run `git pull` before `pr_finish()`, I get the following

```r
Error in git2r::fetch(repo, name = remref_remote(remref), credentials = credentials,  : 
  Error in 'git2r_remote_fetch': 'name' must be a character vector of length one with non NA value
```

1. PR gets merged on GH and the branch is deleted
2. Running `git pull` (the deleted remote branch is fetched)
3. When calling `pr_finish()` now, it errors with the msg above because the remote was removed during the `git pull` call

This happens quite often when working on multiple machines. When finishing the PR on one machine, I do not immediately run `pr_finish()` on the other one. Instead I pull first and then run into the problem described above. 
Happy to do a PR if it would be accepted.

## Proposal

`pr_finish()` should check if the remote still exists and (if not) only delete the local branch.

title: use_github_release() can tag the wrong commit
description:
The `use_github_release()` function creates a draft GitHub Release using the [corresponding GitHub API](https://developer.github.com/v3/repos/releases/#create-a-release). However, it doesn't set the `target_commitish` field and so GitHub uses the default branch (usually `master`).

There are situations where your local HEAD doesn't correspond to the remote default branch. For example, when releasing patches from a non-master branch. In this case, `use_github_release()` checks that local commits have been pushed to the remote, but then tags the wrong commit. I think this function should probably be tagging the most recent local commit.

The docs for use_directory state: "use_directory()` creates a directory (if it does not already exist) in the project's top-level directory."

It would be great if I could do something like:

```
my_dir <- usethis::use_directory("data")
write.csv(file = file.path(my_dir, "somefile.csv"))
```
And have the file appear in "the right place". By the right place I mean the data directory at the top level of my package, whether I'm using devtools::load_all, devtools::install, R CMD INSTALL, etc....

In particular, I want this to work from code that is called via a .onLoad function.

Maybe there's a better way to do this, but I haven't found it yet.

title: README commit hook prevents commit if only .md file changed
description:
When using an `README.Rmd`where the output of chunks can change without changing the code in the `Rmd` file, the commit hook in `usethis::use_readme_rmd` prevents the resulting `README.md` file from being commited to git.

I sometimes add coverage results into the readme during initial development of a package. When knitting the README.Rmd, often only the README.md file changes.

Below is a simple example where the `README.Rmd` file outputs a random number. The commit hook prevents adding a new `README.md` without making a change to `README.Rmd`.

```sh
git init

Rscript -e 'usethis::use_readme_rmd()'

echo '---
output: github_document
---
# my readme
```{r}
runif(1)
```' > README.Rmd

Rscript -e 'knitr::knit("README.Rmd")'

git add README.Rmd README.md
git commit -m "initial commit"

Rscript -e 'knitr::knit("README.Rmd")'

git add README.md
git commit -m "this commit does not work"
```

title: Helpers for GitHub Actions
description:
[GitHub actions](http://github.com/features/actions) is a new workflow automation (~ CI/CD) service from GitHub, still in limited beta as of now.
I think it has some potential for R.

I've written a package for quickly getting started with GitHub actions: [ghactions](http://www.maxheld.de/ghactions/).

It's very closely modelled on usethis, and also includes a front line `ghactions::use_ghactions()` function that writes out sensible defaults for many projects.

It's still very early days for GitHub actions, and ghactions (the pkg) is still maturing.

But *if* things work out and the R community finds GitHub actions helpful, I'd love to write up a short PR wrapping `ghactions::use_ghactions()` in / exporting to `usethis::use_ghactions()` for easier access.

So this will be some time, just wanted to raise this here lest someone else do the same work again.

And also, of course, to gather feedback on [ghactions](http://www.maxheld.de/ghactions/).

title: Allow github_remotes() to search for non-standard github configs
description:
I am using two git profiles on my computer. The one I want to setup with a new package and usethis has the following information in the `/Users/me/.ssh/config` file:

```sh
Host my_other_account
 HostName github.com
 User git
 IdentityFile ~/.ssh/my_other_rsa
```

Since the host name is `my_other_account`, then `usethis:::github_remotes()` does not recognize it as a github remote:
https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/blob/2a862fa9c3420ff9282896331053c9fbaf12a54a/R/github-utils.R#L1-L4
That is, line 2 returns the following, as is intended:
```r
usethis:::github_remotes()
# $origin
# [1] "my_other_account:BarkleyBG/my_repo.git"
```
however, line 4 greps for the phrase `"github"` and fails, even though the git alias is setup correctly.

Major takeaways:
1. Did I miss an existing feature of `usethis` or `remotes` that would help remedy this?
2. Is there a way to programmatically fix this?
3. I did come up with a solution: I changed my `~/.ssh/config` file so that it reads the following way, and I use the second config alias with this repo and it works fine with usethis (so far):

```sh
Host my_other_account
 HostName github.com
 User git
 IdentityFile ~/.ssh/my_other_rsa

Host my_other_github_account
 HostName github.com
 User git
 IdentityFile ~/.ssh/my_other_rsa
```

Thank you for your help! Especially Jenny's in this kind twitter reply: https://twitter.com/JennyBryan/status/1116097484248371201

title: Examples of various ways people use usethis
description:
Preparation for this talk at useR! 2019 Toulouse:

DRY out your workflow with the usethis package
Jenny Bryan
In session "Programming 1", in room Saint-Exupéry
Thursday July 11, 12:06 - 12:24pm (15 mins)

> Usethis is one of the packages created in the recent "conscious uncoupling" of the devtools package. Devtools is an established package that facilitates various aspects of package development. Never fear: devtools is alive and well and remains the public face of this functionality, but it has recently been split into a handful of more focused packages, under the hood. Usethis now holds functionality related to package and project setup. I'll explain the "conscious uncoupling" of devtools and describe the current features of usethis specifically. The DRY concept -- don't repeat yourself -- is well accepted as a best practice for code and it's an equally effective way to approach your development workflow. The usethis package offers functions that enact key steps of the package development process in a programmatic and documented way. This is an attractive alternative to doing everything by hand or, more realistically, copying and modifying files from one of your other packages. Usethis helps with initial setup and also with the sequential addition of features, such as specific dependencies (e.g. Rcpp, the pipe, the tidy eval toolkit) or practices (e.g. version control, testing, continuous integration).

---

I'd like to collect real-world examples of how people-who-are-not-me use usethis!

  * Do you use for day-to-day project setup and maintenance? Which functions are most useful?

  * Have you used it inside a package? What does that package do? Is it somewhere public and OK to mention/link?

  * Have you used it in teaching? How?

Thanks in advance and please include your website (and/or twitter handle or whatever) so that I link to the right "you" in the talk notes and so this thread is more informative.

title: use_github() enterprise API problem
description:
Hi,

I noticed that when trying to us the use_github() function with an enterprise account, it will give me an error saying 
```
Error: GitHub `auth_token` is invalid.
See `browse_github_token()` for help storing a token as an environment variable.
```
After a long search I found out this is because I have an enterprise account through my university and it uses a different host address. When I do use the host api in the function (e.g.  use_github(host = "github.uc.edu/api/v3") ), it still produces the same error.

I know the token is working as I tested it with the gh function:

```r
gh::gh_whoami(.api_url = "https://github.uc.edu/api/v3")
```

I dug in the code and think I found the source of the problem in the following function:

```r
github_user <- function(auth_token = github_token()) {
  suppressMessages(
    tryCatch(gh::gh_whoami(auth_token), error = function(e) NULL)
  )
}
```
This will generate a NULL value if the correct host variable is not given. I think it can simply be fixed by adding the .api_url = host (where host is the variable specified in the use_github ) like so:

```r
github_user <- function(auth_token = github_token()) {
  suppressMessages(
    tryCatch(gh::gh_whoami(auth_token, .api_url = host), error = function(e) NULL)
  )
}
```
Let me know what you think!

Grtz,
PJ
````
