title: `usethis::use_spell_check()` doesn't follow tidyverse style guide and contains lints
description:
Currently, using `usethis::use_spell_check()` creates a new file `spelling.R` with the following code-

```r
if(requireNamespace('spelling', quietly = TRUE))
  spelling::spell_check_test(vignettes = TRUE, error = FALSE,
                             skip_on_cran = TRUE)
```

But, according to the `tidyverse` style guide, the code should instead be-

```r
if (requireNamespace("spelling", quietly = TRUE)) {
  spelling::spell_check_test(
    vignettes = TRUE, error = FALSE,
    skip_on_cran = TRUE
  )
}
```

Additionally, this code also contains the following two lints-

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11330453/62816401-bf8d3600-baf4-11e9-9732-0300e1b5a5ed.png)

It will be neat if `usethis::use_spell_check()` can create the `spelling.R` that avoids both of these issues which will make it easier to not worry about running `styler` after every spellcheck.

title: usethis::use_lifecycle() creates R CMD check note
description:
## Problem
First reported at https://github.com/r-lib/lifecycle/issues/22

`usethis::use_lifecycle()` allows to use `\lifecycle{...}` in function docs. If `lifecycle` is not referenced anywhere else in the package, R CMD check will raise a NOTE.

```r
# develop a package
usethis::use_lifecycle()
# add \lifecycle{...} to some function docs
goodpractice::goodpractice() # raises R CMD check NOTE on unused library `lifecycle`:

N  checking dependencies in R code (401ms)
   Namespace in Imports field not imported from: ‘lifecycle’
     All declared Imports should be used.
```

@lionel- suggested to include a NOOP anywhere in the code:
```
if (FALSE) lifecycle::deprecate_soft()
```

This expression can live in a stand-alone file like [`R/utils-lifecycle.R`](https://github.com/dbca-wa/ruODK/blob/master/R/utils-lifecycle.R).
To preserve test coverage, depending on the coverage tool used, this file should be excluded. For `codecov.io`, this could look like [this](https://github.com/dbca-wa/ruODK/blob/master/codecov.yml#L13). Thinking out loud: it is fine to exclude from tests, as the expression will never run.

As a feature request to `usethis::use_lifecycle()`, could I suggest to 

* generate a file containing a NOOP like `if (FALSE) lifecycle::deprecate_soft()`, and
* exclude that file from whichever test coverage tool is used (or at least message to do so).

``` r

    lapply(c("foo", "bar", "zett"), usethis::use_test) # opens windows in Rstudio (because interactive()  is default)

title: `use_r()` and `use_test()` fail when multiple names are provided in the `name` argument
description:
When providing a vector input with which its length is greater than one, `use_r()` throws a warning and create files with faulty names. For instance;

```r
usethis::use_r(c("fileA", "fileB"))
#> ● Modify 'R/fileA.R', 'R/fileB.NA'
#> Warning messages:
#> 1: In if (!valid_file_name(path_ext_remove(name))) { :
#>   the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used
#> 2: In if (dir_exists(path)) { :
#>   the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used
#> 3: In if (!file.exists(filePath)) { :
#>   the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used
```
Here above, `use_r()` creates two files; the first one is fine, but the second one is created with an `NA` extension. Besides that, such a warning is thrown into the R console.

If we provide the same input to `use_test()`, it fails with the following error message:

```r
usethis::use_test(c("fileA", "fileB"))
#> ✔ Writing 'tests/testthat/test-fileA.R', 'tests/testthat/test-fileB.NA'
#> Error in file(path, open = file_mode, encoding = "utf-8") : 
#>   invalid 'description' argument
#> In addition: Warning messages:
#> 1: In if (!valid_file_name(path_ext_remove(name))) { :
#>   the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used
#> 2: In if (file_exists(proj_path(path))) { :
#>   the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used
#> 3: In if (!file_exists(path)) { :
#>   the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used
#> 4: In if (!file_exists(path)) { :
#>   the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used
```

At the first glance, the problem seems to happen around that call, `check_file_name()`, which is placed in the `R/r.R` file.

The usethis version I run is `1.5.1.9000`.

title: PR vignette use case fails behind authenticated PROXY

title: Feature Request: use_operator() for general operator importing.
description:
Note: I've suggested this once before in [`devtools`](https://github.com/r-lib/devtools/issues/1593) but didn't get any interest.

The idea is for a more generic version of `use_pipe` that takes any operator and package as arguments. 

For example:

```r
use_operator(operator = `%<-%`, package = "zeallot", dependency = "Imports", export = TRUE)
```

Would have the following effects:

* `zeallot` is added to DESCRIPTION under "Imports" (if not already in DESCRIPTION)
* an R is created file that makes `%<-%` available, e.g.:

```

title: Be explicit about when just cloning (as vs. forking + cloning) with create_from_github()
description:
It's frustrating when you think you've forked and cloned a repo, but you've only just cloned the repo, because you don't have a Github PAT set up (or you normally use SSH, so `create_from_github()` doesn't quite work for you from the outset...). 

Could there be a check/warning added in the `create_from_github()` function to see if you have a Github PAT in your .Renviron, and some message in red saying "NOTE: you don't have a Github PAT, so you will just clone this package, rather than forking + cloning it"? It could also be an numbered/"select this" option, but that would probably be annoying for most users who've already set up the PAT.

title: Documentation says "activate a package"
description:
The documentation for `create_tidy_package` says it "activates" the package:

https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/blob/master/R/tidyverse.R#L11

Packages cannot be activated. Projects can. I know its probably pedantry but I can't help myself...

Suggest either rename the function to `create_tidy_project` or change the documentation to indicate this also makes an RStudio *project* skeleton and activates that.

(Its a shame that lots of the useful functionality of `devtools` and `usethis` are becoming project-oriented and less useful to anyone trying to do less opinionated package development)

![snippet](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12725868/64560891-1daa7480-d352-11e9-8e72-c3a2fb27c33f.png)

title: usethis::use_ccby_license() creates a "non-standard license specification" that is not "standardizable" by devtools::check()
description:
To create a reproducible example, I used `usethis::create_package()` to create a blank template package.

```r
usethis::create_package(path = "issue")
```

Then, in the new package project, I used `usethis::use_ccby_license()` to use the CC BY-SA 4.0 license. I need to use this license, as my package relies on some data under this same license.

``` r
packageVersion("devtools")
#> [1] '2.2.0'
packageVersion("usethis")
#> [1] '1.5.1'
usethis::use_ccby_license(name = "Kiernan Nicholls")
devtools::check()
```

This `devtools::check()` returns a warning, as the license is apparently non-standard.

```
── R CMD check results ── issue 0.0.0.9000 ──
Duration: 3.1s

❯ checking DESCRIPTION meta-information ... WARNING
  Non-standard license specification:
    CCBY-4.0
  Standardizable: FALSE

0 errors ✔ | 1 warning ✖ | 0 notes ✔
```

I'm following along in the [R Packages book](https://r-pkgs.org/), which says this warning would prevent my package from being released to CRAN.

> If you want to release your package to CRAN, you must pick a standard license. Otherwise it’s difficult for CRAN to determine whether or not it’s legal to distribute your package! You can find a complete list of licenses that CRAN considers valid at https://svn.r-project.org/R/trunk/share/licenses/license.db.

Going to that link, CC BY-SA 4.0 is listed as a valid license (and all other CC BY-SA versions recommend CC BY-SA 4.0)

> Name: Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License
> Abbrev: CC BY-SA 4.0
> FSF: free_and_GPLv3_incompatible
> URL: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
> FOSS: yes
> Extensible: yes

title: Optionally allow non-CRAN names in create_package and use_description
description:
It's often useful to have package structures or even just DESCRIPTION files in projects that aren't fully packages or will never go to a repository, but the namespace is only so big and underscores/dashes are useful in project names.  I would like a `check_name=TRUE` argument for `use_description()` and `create_package()` so I can skip the name-checking error and use these functions for more projects.  It could also default to `getOptions(usethis.checkname)`

Happy to write the PR for this if you think the feature should exist.

title: Authentication error when using pr_init()
description:
I'm working through the nice new pull request helpers vignette and have run into a problem when attempting to use `pr_init()`.

I am on a Windows 7 machine and use SSH transport protocol.  `git2r::cred_ssh_key()` returns the correct info so I use `use_git_credentials(credentials = git2r::cred_ssh_key())` prior to forking and cloning with `create_from_github()` to successfully clone a repo.

However, in the next step, where I make a branch with `pr_init()`, I get an authentication error from `git2r::fetch()` (after setting my credentials again with `use_git_credentials()`).

```r
pr_init("makenew")
✔ Checking that local branch 'master' has the changes in 'origin/master'
Error in git2r::fetch(repo, name = remref_remote(remref), refspec = branch,  : 
  Error in 'git2r_remote_fetch': error authenticating: failed connecting agent
```

After poking through the innards of `pr_init()`, I *think* this error may be stemming from `git_branch_compare()`.  This function relies on `git2r::fetch()` but never sets up the credentials for fetching.  I can reproduce the error by running `git_branch_compare()` directly.

```r
usethis:::git_branch_compare("master")
Error in git2r::fetch(repo, name = remref_remote(remref), refspec = branch,  : 
  Error in 'git2r_remote_fetch': error authenticating: failed connecting agent
```

If I add a line like `credentials = git_credentials()` within `git2r::fetch()` in `git_branch_compare()` I get output instead of an error.  I don't know if credentials should need to be explicitly set in `git2r::fetch()` or not.  If not, I may have something else going on with my credentials set-up.

title: use_build_ignore generates invalid regular expression
description:
When using a wildcard in the files argument the use_build_ignore function generates invalid regex.

For example `use_build_ignore("*.xlsx")` will print `Adding '^*\\.xlsx$' to '.Rbuildignore'` in the console but in fact adds `^*\.xlsx$` (note the difference) which will break devtools::check(). Either way, I believe both are invalid. I believe the correct regex would be `^.*\.xlsx$`. 

What I was trying to do was to ignore all Excel files. There might be some reason not use a wildcard, but in that case the function should just print an error or warning. 

```r
usethis::use_build_ignore("*.xlsx")
```

title: use_tutorial() creates file in wrong location and ignores html built files, but run_tutorial() requires it
description:
`use_tutorial()` creates R Markdown files in `inst/tutorials/` as single files. But learnr requires them in individual folders:

> Create a tutorials directory within the inst sub-directory of your package and then create a directory for your tutorial there (e.g. inst/tutorials/hello, inst/tutorials/slidy, etc.). https://rstudio.github.io/learnr/publishing.html

Likewise, `use_tutorial()` adds git ignore to the generated html tutorials, but learnr requires the html files to be present: 

> Render your tutorial .Rmd to .html and include the rendered HTML in your R package (this will happen automatically during development & preview of the tutorial, you just need to be sure to include the .html file within the R package when you build it). https://rstudio.github.io/learnr/publishing.html

So when you run `run_tutorials()` for the tutorial, you get:

``` r
> learnr::run_tutorial("chapter1", package = "acdcourse")
Error in shiny_prerendered_html(input_rmd, encoding, render_args) : 
  Prerendered HTML file not found at ./chapter1.html
```

Not sure if there is a disconnect between usethis and learnr or if learnr intends to go the route as indicated by `use_tutorial()`.

title: provide possibility to reorder package names in use_package
description:
As @hadley writes in [Section 5.1 of R Packages](https://r-pkgs.org/description.html#dependencies)

> Both Imports and Suggests take a comma separated list of package names.
> I recommend putting one package on each line, and keeping them in alphabetical order.
> That makes it easy to skim.
> 

while developing a package it makes life easier to have the packages in Imports/Suggests/...
sorted alphabetically 

I would suggest to extend `use_package` with an extra argument in order to also make it
possible sort the packages.
The default value `sort = FALSE` would reproduce current behavior
```
use_package <- function(package, type = "Imports", min_version = NULL, sort = FALSE)
```
while `sort = TRUE` would also sort the packages within the relevant `type`, i.e. something
like the following inside `use_dependency` could do the trick:

```
rest_deps <-  deps %>% filter(type != type)
type_deps <- deps %>% filter(type == type) %>% arrange(package)
# put them together
deps <- type_deps %>% bind_rows(rest_deps)
```

Someone at the workshop used a proxy but did not have their environment variables set up for the proxy. I think that proxy-setup is clearly beyond the scope of usethis, but it did seem that from the `git_sitrep()` perspective, a network failure is indistinguishable from an invalid token.

With my network off:

``` r
usethis::git_sitrep()

title: use_roxygen_md() provides wrong message for using roxygen2md()
description:
`use_roxygen_md()` gives the output:

```
● Run the following code, then rerun `devtools::document()`
  roxygen2md::roxygen2md("/home/luke/Desktop/zipffreq")
  [Copied to clipboard]
```

But `roxygen2md::roxygen2md()` docs say it only takes the `scope` argument:

> roxygen2md(scope = c("full", "simple", "none"))
> 
> `scope`: The scope of transformations: "simple" runs only transformations that shouldn't substantially change the resulting .Rd files, "full" runs all transformations. In larger packages, run "none", double-check and track the changes, and then run "simple" and then "full".

I assume `use_roxygen_md()` should give:

```
● Run the following code, then rerun `devtools::document()`
  roxygen2md::roxygen2md("full")
  [Copied to clipboard]
```

Or maybe `"simple"` instead of `"full"`.

Versions:

```
> packageVersion("roxygen2md")
[1] ‘1.0.0’
> packageVersion("usethis")
[1] ‘1.5.0’
```

title: Could use_roxygen_md() give more info on roxygen2md package?
description:
This is one of the feedbacks from a successful workshop where we used **usethis 1.5.0**.

If you create a package from nothing, using `create_package()`, then `document()` it before calling `use_roxygen_md()`, you get in a situation where you get the **roxygen2md** message:

https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/blob/a7d6eb42d457e893f384bc9788a0b931bfef4479/R/roxygen.R#L19

Because the roxygen2md package is not (yet ?) on CRAN, it might be useful to provide explicit feedback that you will have to use something like `devtools::install_github("r-lib/roxygen2md")`. 

I see that this is implied in the function documentation for `use_roxygen_md()`.

Also, if roxygen2md will be on CRAN in the near future, perhaps this issue takes care of itself.

---

One possible solution may be to add an optional `msg` argument to the internal function `check_package()`.

Happy to make a PR following any approach you may suggest.

title: feature request: `use_tidy_api()` function to make API files
description:
Recently I have started to notice `API` files in `tidyverse` packages (e.g., [dplyr](https://github.com/rstudio/gt/blob/master/API), [gt](https://github.com/tidyverse/dplyr/blob/master/API), etc.) and was wondering if you would consider adding support for making such files in a function like `use_tidy_api()`? 

Currently, there doesn't seem to be a unified way to do it. Some people seem to use `pkgapi::extract_api()`, while others use `pkgattrs::write_pkg_api()`. 

The problem with the former is that it doesn't generate a file, but rather outputs the `API` as text which needs to be copied to `API` file. This means the API file needs to be manually generated after every single change to the package API.

The latter _does_ generate a file but doesn't seem to be working and the repo has been inactive for a while (https://github.com/rich-iannone/pkgattrs/issues/1).

title: create_from_github() on Windows
description:
As @jennybc has mentioned elsewhere, getting R to work programmatically with GitHub on Windows can be a pain. Part of that pain stems from setting up ssh keys and making sure that git2r knows where to find them. I wrote the following gist, which is a aggregation of resources found in various usethis docs and #711. 

In light of @jennybc's message on Twitter (https://twitter.com/JennyBryan/status/1124346858841595905), my initial sense is to add more description to the docs on `create_from_github()` rather than create a separate function. Perhaps a Windows-specific note on how users might need to make explicit use of `use_git_credentials()`. What are your thoughts? I'd be happy to submit a PR. 

```r
prep_for_pr <- function(username, repo_spec){

use_git_protocol("ssh")
  
creds <- cred_ssh_key(publickey = glue("C:/Users/{username}/.ssh/id_rsa.pub"),
                      privatekey = glue("C:/Users/{username}/.ssh/id_rsa"), 
                      passphrase = character(0))    

use_git_credentials(credentials = creds)

create_from_github(glue("{repo_spec}", 
                   destdir = "C:/Users/{username}/Desktop"))
} 

prep_for_pr("chrisengelhardt", "r-lib/usethis")
```

title: Have `usethis::proj_path_prep()` use `fs::path_abs(fs::path_expand())` instead of `fs::path_real()`
description:
usethis currently uses `fs::path_real()` to determine the project path, however this poses problems when the path is a mapped network drive on Windows, because the root no longer can be calculated relative to the input path.

I map my R projects folder to my windows VM, so I run into this situation often.

I propose to instead use `fs::path_abs(fs::path_expand())`.

``` r
usethis::proj_set("Z:/projects/remotes")
#>  Setting active project to '//vmware-host/Shared Folders/projects/remotes'
usethis::use_test()
#> Error: Open file must be in the 'R/' directory of the active package.
#> * Actual path: 'Z:/projects/remotes/R/submodule.R'
fs::path_real("Z:/projects/remotes/R/submodule.R")
#> //vmware-host/Shared Folders/projects/remotes/R/submodule.R
fs::path_abs(fs::path_expand("Z:/projects/R/submodule.R"))
#> Z:/projects/R/submodule.R

fs::path_real("~/Links")
#> C:/Users/IEUser/Links
fs::path_abs(fs::path_expand("~/Links"))
#> C:/Users/IEUser/Links
```

Created on 2018-10-12 by the [reprex package](http://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.2.0).

title: create_from_github(): ensure forked repos are current with upstream/master
description:
Follow-on from #685.

> If I `create_from_github()` on someone else's repository for which I already have a GitHub fork (e.g. `r-lib/usethis`), the copy that gets cloned to my computer is my master branch, not the upstream master branch. I will probably want to start my work from the upstream master, rather than my likely-stale master. I know that this is easily fixed with `pr_pull_upstream()`, but I wonder if this might be a useful default behavior for `create_from_github()`.

It would seem to be a matter of adding  `pr_pull_upstream()` to the end of:

https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/blob/274902535ea489dbaa4b57e56ad8c6d81e62a988/R/create.R#L198-L202

I'm assuming that the feedback (`ui_done()`) from `pr_pull_upstream()` takes care of having to add something here ourselves.

I'll start a PR for this, subject to your guidance.

title: feature request: use_openmp()
description:
OpenMP can be a major performance factor in some applications, and also a frequent cause of misery in setting up Makevars, as evidenced by various stackoverflow questions.

https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/issues/688 about RcppEigen and openmp is somewhat related. Having `use_openmp()` would transfer responsibility for OpenMP activation to the user, rather than `use_rcpp_eigen()` potentially doing it for them.

I've personally had a bad interaction between CRAN's solaris testing and OpenMP in a C++11 enabled package a couple of years ago. I don't know where this stands now, but `usethis` could check for this kind of thing, and warn or stop on such interactions, again helping the end user avoid hours of trial-and-error with CRAN or searching the web.

This could also make a skeleton C or C++ file (or Fortran!) with OpenMP pragmas defined for a simple loop.

title: use_rcpp_eigen should add openmp makevars
description:
https://eigen.tuxfamily.org/dox/TopicMultiThreading.html describes enabling `openmp` on compilation for multi-threaded optimization of many of the key operations which Eigen offers. `use_rcpp_eigen` does not do this, whereas `use_rcpp_armadillo` does. Unlike Armadillo, Eigen does not need BLAS, LAPACK.

Can I suggest the following:
```
PKG_CPPFLAGS=-DEIGEN_PERMANENTLY_DISABLE_STUPID_WARNINGS $(SHLIB_OPENMP_CXXFLAGS)
PKG_LIBS=$(SHLIB_OPENMP_CXXFLAGS)
```

title: pr_*() lifecycle leaves empty sections behind in .git/config
description:
After copious use of the `pr_*()` family, here's look at usethis's `.git/config`:

```
[core]
	repositoryformatversion = 0
	filemode = true
	bare = false
	logallrefupdates = true
	ignorecase = true
	precomposeunicode = true
[remote "origin"]
	url = git@github.com:r-lib/usethis.git
[branch "master"]
[branch "f-479-proj-path-prep"]
[branch "ui-path-abs"]
[branch "pr-update-source"]
[branch "stufield-issue-581"]
[branch "angela-li-use-tutorial"]
[branch "pr-love-for-https"]
[branch "release-type"]
[branch "njtierney-add-ccby"]
[branch "cwickham-use-course-links"]
[branch "khailper-tidy-dev-day-issue-526-take-2"]
[branch "overmar-gitlab-ci"]
[branch "bugfix/brach-with-slash"]
[branch "refactor-github-token"]
[branch "pr-sitrep"]
[remote "origin"]
	fetch = +refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*
[branch "master"]
	remote = origin
	merge = refs/heads/master
[branch "remote-management"]
[remote "nijibabulu"]
	url = git@github.com:nijibabulu/usethis.git
	fetch = +refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/nijibabulu/*
[branch "nijibabulu-master"]
```

Note the empty sections related to branches that no longer exist. They are harmless but, in the limit, this will have to be cleaned out. It's not immediately clear to me that usethis can do this. So I'm opening and then closing this, just to record what I know.

SO thread about this general problem with git config, which is allegedly somewhat better in very recent versions of git (the relevant commits are from ~April 2018):

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/15935624/how-do-i-avoid-empty-sections-when-removing-a-setting-from-git-config

Old libgit2 thread that ends with no action (we would have to do this libgit2, mediated by git2r):

https://github.com/libgit2/libgit2/issues/1205

title: Function to do the remote rename dance
description:
When people first start contributing to a package one of the first major roadblocks is they likely have cloned the repo from the initial repo rather than from a fork. So they have to 

1) rename the origin remote to upstream then add the new remote as origin
2) or burn it all down and re-clone from their fork, then add the origin as upstream later.

As far as I know there is no real way to do either step without needing command line git or something like Sourcetree, so it ends up being a pretty big hurdle for new contributors.

title: pr_push() and / in branches

I'm not sure how to create a reprex for this, so I'll explain. I'm trying to push into that pr: https://github.com/apache/arrow/pull/3932

It looks like the `git_parse_remref` does not want branch names with a `/`

function (remref) 
{

title: use_package_doc: prefill from DESCRIPTION
description:
This feature request suggests adapting the template for package-level documentation. The DESCRIPTION file already provides a title and description for a package. It should be relatively straightforward to utilize these entries in the `use_package_docs()` templates as `@title` and `@description`. For example.

```r
#' @importFrom desc desc_get_field
use_package_doc <- function() {
  check_is_package("use_package_doc()")
  use_template(
    "packagename-package.R", 
    package_doc_path(), 
    data = list(
      title = desc_get_field("Title"),
      description = desc_get_field("description")
    )
  )
}
```

First lines of the template:

```
#' @title {{{ title }}}
#' @description {{{ description }}}
"_Package"
```

The current template provides no hints how the final roxygen block should look like. Also, it seems most r-lib and tidyverse packages are consistent between the DESCRIPTION file and the package-level documentation in that regard. This feature would encourage other package authors to adapt this consistency.

If this feature is considered worthwhile, I can submit a PR with a new implementation of `inst/templates/packagename-package.R` and `use_package_doc()`.

title: Predictable Answers to use_course() Prompts
description:
I had a [quick exchange](https://twitter.com/JennyBryan/status/1098391788694323200) with @jennybc on Twitter today about the way that `use_course()` answers appear in "random" fashion:

```
> usethis::use_course("https://github.com/slu-dss/wrangling-01/archive/master.zip")
 Downloaded: 2.06 MB  
A ZIP file named:
  'wrangling-01-master.zip'
will be copied to this folder:
  '/Users/chris/Desktop'
Prefer a different location? Cancel, try again, and specify `destdir`.

Is it OK to write this file here?
1: No way
2: No
3: I agree
```

I have been using `use_course()` for teaching the last few semesters and it solves a lot of issues we've dealt with in the past. The unpredictable way that answers to "Is it OK to write this file here?" are presented seems to throw folks off - it's harder for us to provide guidance beyond "answer in the affirmative" to each question. 

I'm happy to put together a PR that adds a `ui_yeah_simple()` function to `ui.R` that presents only "Yes" and "No" as options in the same order each time. I'd then update `use_course()` to use the simplified version rather than `ui_yeah()`. Wanted to open up an issue for discussion before I dug into this, though!

title: Link to obvious places in R Packages and WRE from help files
Stale Bot
description:
Issue open from #593 to add `use_*bot` functions, such as Stale bot: https://github.com/apps/stale.

This issue is to open the discussion of bots, not necessarily enable the `use_stale` rejected PR from below.  Overall, this discussion should at least cover:

1.  Should bots be in `usethis` for `use_*` functions
2. How should `.github` be incorporated into the creation.  Such as, I'm not sure if `use_github` should create `.github` folder and put in `.Rbuildignore`.
3. Should template go in `inst/templates` like others?


---

Example of `inst/templates/stale.yml`:
```yml
# Number of days of inactivity before an issue becomes stale
daysUntilStale: 60
# Number of days of inactivity before a stale issue is closed
daysUntilClose: 7
# Issues with these labels will never be considered stale
exemptLabels:
  - pinned
  - security
# Label to use when marking an issue as stale
staleLabel: wontfix
# Comment to post when marking an issue as stale. Set to `false` to disable
markComment: >
  This issue has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had
  recent activity. It will be closed if no further activity occurs. Thank you
  for your contributions.
# Comment to post when closing a stale issue. Set to `false` to disable
closeComment: false
```

Here is an example of the docs for `R/stale.R`.
```r
#' Add Stale Bot
#'
#' `use_stale()` Adds [GitHub Stale Bot](https://github.com/apps/stale) to
#' add Stale bot to your repository
#'
#' @inheritParams use_template
#' @export
use_stale <- function(open = interactive()) {
  check_uses_github()
  if (!dir.exists(".github")) {
    dir.create(".github", showWarnings = FALSE)
    usethis::use_build_ignore(".github")
  }
  new <- use_template(
    "stale.yml",
    ".github/stale.yml",
    ignore = TRUE,
    open = open
  )
  if (open) {
    utils::browseURL("https://github.com/apps/stale")
  }
  if (!new) return(invisible(FALSE))

  invisible(TRUE)
}
```

title: Delete CRAN-RELEASE
description:
The checklist created by `use_release_issue()` prompts you to use `devtools::submit_cran()`, which creates a file named CRAN-RELEASE with contents like this:

```
This package was submitted to CRAN on 2019-02-14.
Once it is accepted, delete this file and tag the release (commit f3bdd61d8e).

description:

title: `git_vaccinate()` drops blank lines and repeated comments
description:
`git_vaccinate()` calls `write_union()` to update the global gitignore file and `write_union()` keeps only unique lines.

https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/blob/e9a3c8299c132f9fc8a630886e26c36668f427c7/R/write.R#L61

Unfortunately this deletes all empty lines (but the first) and repeated comments, such as those often used around section headings, e.g.

```
value = 123

########################
# A new section        #
########################

value2 = 456
```

Becomes

```
value = 123

########################
# A new section        #
value2 = 456
```

Since you are already doing a set diff of the new lines and the existing lines, couldn't you just prepend the new lines rather than taking the union to avoid this? e.g. change that line to

```r
all <- c(new, existing_lines)
```

title: `usethis::use_test()` does not remain true to original *.R open source file name
description:
With `use_test()`, if the current source editor file name is, e.g. camel case, the `test-*.R` file that is created is converted to all lower case with a call to `tolower()`. I think this is making an unnecessary decision for the user. Additionally, if the user tries to force the file name by passing a `name =` argument, this is also converted to lower case.

Example of the problem with default:
```r
source editor filename: "my_coolFunctionPrint.R"
use_test()
resulting test: "test-my_coolfunctionprint.R"
```
Example of the problem with `name = ***` passed:
```r
source editor filename: "my_coolFunctionPrint.R"
use_test("theBestFunctionEver")
resulting test: "test-thebestfunctionever.R"
```

This is likely unnoticed if strict adherence to the Tidyverse style guide, but other style guides will break the filename.R -> test-filename.R pattern. There appears to be a `tolower()` call somewhere converting the case that needs some conditional logic to it. I'd be happy to submit a PR if necessary.

title: use_build_ignore(): Handle directories specially
description:
Not a bug, but an idea for possible enhancement to `use_build_ignore()`.

Currently, all arguments to `use_build_ignore` are terminated with a `$` before being written to `.Rbuildignore`. This is helpful for individual files. However, If any argument is a directory, the result is not what I expected: none of the contents of the directory are ignored.

One mitigation that comes to mind is to test each `file` and determine if it's a directory. If it is, don't terminate its `.Rbuildignore` line with `$`. I'm happy to contribute a PR to do this if one is desired.

```r
# create a directory
dir.create("foob")
# ignore it
usethis::use_build_ignore("foob")
# observe that ^foob$ has been added (which will not match the contents of foob/)
file.show(".Rbuildignore")
```

title: use_pkgdown_travis() lacks some detail
description:
~I have not yet succeeded~ but want to record some notes as I go.

`ui_todo("Create gh-pages branch")` is a bit of an understatement. In greater detail:

1. Quit any RStudio instance in the target project. You don't want a lock on any hidden files used by RStudio that will diminish the effect of the recursive file removal we're about to do.
2. In the shell, in the target repo (in fact, I suspect this should be `rm -rf .` 😬) ... *Update: I now see that these git instructions are given in `pkgdown::deploy_site_github()`. It would be a great idea to link to that!* It's really important that this branch be completely empty. I learned this the hard way.

You need to make sure the repo's settings re: GitHub Pages are correct, i.e. set to `gh-pages branch`.

The `before_deploy` and `deploy` blocks for insertion into `.travis.yml` need to be inserted into the build matrix, presumably for `r: release`.

For tidyverse packages only, tidytemplate needs to be installed from GitHub.

title: pr_* does not work with non ssh credentials
description:
Macro issue is #534 

While testing those new functions, I have seen that `pr_push` does not work when your are not using ssh credential. 

```r
> usethis::pr_push()
✔ Checking that 'fix/155-paste-oracle' branch is up to date
✔ Pushing changes to GitHub PR
Error in git2r::push(git_repo(), name = name, refspec = paste0("refs/heads/",  : 
  Error in 'git2r_push': Unable to authenticate with supplied credentials
```

By default git2r uses ssh, and for other auth mechanisms, a credential object should be pass in each function. It is not possible to setup globally at the moment (see ropensci/git2r#337)

While this is not supported in git2r, usethis could create the `git2r::cred_token` if a GITHUB_PAT exists and use it each time it is needed when remote is https.

title: use_readme_rmd ingests git hook
description:
Currently `use_readme_rmd()` does ingest a pre commit Git hook into the package's local git repository. There are two problems resulting from this: (1) This hook also prevents updates of the repo when the Rmd-file is simply re-rendered (e.g. automatically obtained information is updated). (2) User are neither informed about the ingestion happening and have no possibility to prevent it. 

This is related to the discussion found here https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/issues/312 and to that found here https://twitter.com/jeroenhjanssens/status/1075010648587886592.

I have forked this repo and will file a pull request with a possible solution that will ...

1. allow users to opt in or opt out per function argument, 
2. will default to opt out in non-interactive environments, 
3. will ask user what to do in case of an interactive session, 
4. and will have tests covering the new adopted behaviour.

title: Making pr_*() functions work for anyone besides Hadley 😇
description:
I'm trying out the workflow with a PR in readr.

My local readr repo is the active usethis project.

My remote situation:

```
jenny@2015-mbp readr $ git remote -v
origin  https://github.com/jennybc/readr.git (fetch)
origin  https://github.com/jennybc/readr.git (push)
upstream        https://github.com/tidyverse/readr.git (fetch)
upstream        https://github.com/tidyverse/readr.git (push)
```

That is: `origin` is my fork and `upstream` is the main repo.

`pr_fetch(933)` fails here for me:

```
>   pr <- gh::gh("GET /repos/:owner/:repo/pulls/:number",
+     owner = github_owner(),
+     repo = github_repo(),
+     number = number
+   )
Error in gh_process_response(raw) :

Message: Not Found
Read more at https://developer.github.com/v3/pulls/#get-a-single-pull-request

URL not found: https://api.github.com/repos/jennybc/readr/pulls/933
```

because it tries to get the PR from my fork instead of the main repo. We have to be fork-savvy re: `owner`. Shortly thereafter, this also influences the `user` object that is the name of the remote where the PR lives.

title: Re-export := with use_tidy_eval
description: := (the tidyeval assignment operator, which I pronounce "digested is") is often as useful for tidyeval as the functions exported by the file generated via usethis::use_tidyeval(). It would be helpful if it were also re-exported.

title: Allow to use capital letters when using use_r
description:
I was surprised that I couldn't create the AllGenerics.R file via the `use_r` function, because it converts all the names to lower case. The reason is that it uses `slug` calls `asciify` which converts everything to lower case:

https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/blob/02fc4b20f022b0b98afcb323ef770fd78c00ae5a/R/utils.R#L33

The tidyverse [naming conventions](https://style.tidyverse.org/files.html#names) recommend the "all-generics.R" style. But in other styles ([Bioconductor](https://bioconductor.org/developers/how-to/coding-style/)) it is recommended to use the CamelCase format for some files like this one. Perhaps `use_r` could allow file names in upper case too? (Maybe with a warning?)


I could submit a pull request (or leave it for the developer conference day) if you wish.

title: use_github(): be more resilient to partial setup
description:
Right now it is possible for `use_github()` to successfully create a GitHub repo and set a remote. But then fail to push, e.g. due to SSH key/passphrase problems.

Then, when you call it again, it exits early, because it thinks the repo already uses GitHub, because the remote is set. If you unset that, you get a new (cryptic) error because the remote repo already exists.

Could it handle "partial setup" better?

title: consider putting `install_cran("pkgdown)` in `before_cache` rather than `before_deploy`
description:
`use_pkgdown()` recommends you put `remotes::install_cran("pkgdown")` in `before_deploy`. This works well, the only issue is because the package cache is uploaded _before_ the before_deploy stage happens pkgdown and its dependencies will not be in the cache. If `pkgdown` is a normal dependency of the package (such as in the usethis pkg itself) this isn't a problem, but if your package would not normally depend on pkgdown it will be.

Putting the install command instead in `before_cache` would cause it to run right before the cache is uploaded, which would cause the packages to be included in the cache. The cache is only updated on successful builds, so I think this will do what we want.

The main downside to this approach is it is more confusing, but I think likely it is worthwhile...

However, the function `code_block()` for formatting and accessing the clipboard is not exported currently. Are there plans to export `code_block()` in the future so we can create generic `use_usethis`-esque functions? Or perhaps create some kind of API for creating generic `use_` functions, maybe by way of a closure/function factory?

```r
use_ <- function(edit_function, todo_text, code, ...) {
    function() {
        edit_function(...)
        todo(todo_text)
        code_block(code)
    }
}

use_x <- use_(edit_r_profile,
             todo_text = "Include this code in your .Rprofile to get x package working",
             code = c(".Last <- function() {", "message('All done.')", "}")
```

title: use_article()
description:
We need `use_article()` which is a minor variant on `use_vignette()`.

What's wrong with using `use_vignette()` to create an article?

  1. If you *only* have articles, you want to Rbuildignore the directory that contains them. So either `vignettes/` or `vignettes/articles/`.
  2. Creation of an article should never trigger an edit to DESCRIPTION. Specifically, do not add a `VignetteBuilder` field.
  3. The article itself should not have a `vignettes:` section in the yaml header.

To see me recovering from all of the above mistakes, look at these travis ci reports:

title: Add setup code for CI with tic
description:
The [_travis_ package]() communicates with the Travis API v3 and supports, among others, enabling and disabling a repository, and adding public or private environment variables. The [_tic_ package](https://ropenscilabs.github.io/tic/) implements a CI-agnostic DSL for defining CI runs. Ultimately, most of the logic from Travis's [`r.rb`](https://github.com/travis-ci/travis-build/blob/master/lib/travis/build/script/r.rb) could be provided by _tic_.

Currently, the setup code for adding _tic_ support to a package lives in _travis_. It consists of:

- Code to enable the repo on Travis
- Code to add an SSH key as encrypted environment variable and add a deploy key to GitHub, to enable automatic deployment from Travis
- Template files for `tic.R` for various use cases (package checks, blogdown, bookdown, ...)
- Template files for _tic_-style `.travis.yml` and `appveyor.yml` (same for all project types)

I'd like to suggest to move this setup code to _usethis_, and provide an alternative to `use_travis()` and `use_appveyor()` that would set up this "new-style" CI. The old functions would remain until _tic_ becomes the recommended way for CI in R.

Even if we only wanted to use the "enable Travis" feature, work must be done because currently _travis_ imports _usethis_.

Existing PR: #411.

Reference: https://github.com/ropenscilabs/travis/issues/73

CC @hadley @karthik @pat-s.

title: Adapt to travis policy changes for open source project on travis-ci.com
description:
Hi, 

working on a new package I found that travis has just change its policy for open source project. See the blog post [Announcing support for open source projects on travis-ci.com](https://blog.travis-ci.com/2018-05-02-open-source-projects-on-travis-ci-com-with-github-apps)

Currently, `use_travis()` create a badge using `use_travis_badge()` only towards _travis-ci.org_ only. 
As the platform _.com_ is planned to be the only one and considering that travis advice to open new project on _travis-ci.com_,it could be interesting to integrate that into {usethis} function. 

Maybe an argument for choosing the site could help.
```r
use_badge_travis <- function (ext= c("com", "org")) 
{
  ext<- match.arg(ext)
  website <- paste0("https://travis-ci.", ext)
  gh <- gh::gh_tree_remote(proj_get())
  url <- file.path(website, gh$username, gh$repo)
  img <- paste0(url, ".svg?branch=master")
  use_badge("Travis build status", url, img)
}

# keep the current behaviour as default.
use_travis <- function (browse = interactive(), ext= "org") 
{
  check_uses_github()
  use_template("travis.yml", ".travis.yml", ignore = TRUE)
  travis_activate(browse)
  use_travis_badge(ext= ext)
  invisible(TRUE)
}
```

Currently, I see no other change other than the fact that `travis-ci.com` doesn't work with codecov without setting a token. I opened issues towards travis and codecov to see if this will change or not.

I opened this issue more to keep that travis change in mind and discuss it than to provide a change in {usethis} quickly. This could definitively wait.

title: more convenient TDD support
description:
Hello and 1k thanks for working on simplifying R package development :-)

In the [test-driven development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Test_driven_development) model/philosophy, tests are written before the code, so that the latter fulfills what the former specify. Currently, [`usethis` supports this by calling `use_r()` without parameter](https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/commit/c5399df2788483c406561b9a3d4703ddb0ab9a03) to open the corresponding `.R` file from within an active `test-...R` file.

How about a parameter like `TDD = TRUE` in both or either [`use_r()`](https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/blob/master/R/r.R) and [`use_test()`](https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/blob/master/R/test.R#L24) (or a new function `use_TDD("function_name")`!) that:

a) creates both files, but
b) opens `test-function_name.R` last, so that the cursor focus is there first.

The user would need only one function call, then code the tests first and conveniently switch to the already prepared `function_name.R`.

Cheers :-)

title: Allow multiple scripts to be applied for the same git hook
description:
When I apply `use_git_hook()` to apply multiple scripts to the same git hook, I get the following error:

```
usethis::use_git_hook("pre-commit", system.file("templates", "readme-rmd-pre-commit.sh", package = "usethis"))
  usethis::use_git_hook("pre-commit", system.file("templates", "description-codemetajson-pre-commit.sh", package = "codemetar"))
```
```
Writing '.git/hooks/pre-commit'
Error: '.git/hooks/pre-commit' already exists.
```
I believe this is because git only allows one script per hook type.  A possible solution is for usethis to have a _general_ hook script which calls any other script one applies via `use_git_hook()`, or perhaps append the script.  In this case [`description-codemetajson-pre-commit.sh`](https://github.com/ropensci/codemetar/blob/master/inst/templates/description-codemetajson-pre-commit.sh), is very similar to the usethis README hook - it checks that `codemeta.json` is updated after `DESCRIPTION.`

CC @maelle @cboettig

title: Allow directory creation with use_course
description:
If would be handy if `use_course` got an addition argument to create (recursively) the directory specified in `destdir` if it doesn't exist already. This would be especially useful when multiple faculty are using the same server and want to give students a little nudge to put the project folders in a relevant class directory. On Windows or Mac it is easy for students to drag a folder where they want it. However, on this is a bit more work for students new to Rstudio server for example

What I have in mind would be to share something like the commands below with students to ensure that the project folder goes into a class directory. The directory `class124/session` would be created on the fly as needed. Of course the student could always change the `dest` if they want.

`usethis::use_course("https://link.to.a.project.folder2", dest = "~/class124/session1", create = TRUE)`
`usethis::use_course("https://link.to.a.project.folder2", dest = "~/class124/session1", create = TRUE)`

I could also add something like the below to the code to share with students but the additional attribute for `use_course` seems nicer ... at least to me

`if (!dir.exists("~/class124/session1")) dir.create("~/class124/session1", recursive = TRUE)`

title: Get rid of rematch2 dependency ... maybe?
default to not running spell check tests on CRAN servers
description:
I have been using `usethis::use_spell_check()` to check spellings. But this creates a test that is good to run locally but not suitable for CRAN. My package has been rejected twice because of the spelling tests with the following comment-

> why do you run spell check in the tests?
> 
> Spelling won't change, hence no need to run that daily on several 
> machines on CRAN. Just do it once prior to submission.
> 
> In tests, the idea is to check whether your package is calculating 
> correctly which may change due to changes on the operating systems, in 
> R, or package dependencies.

What can I do to not run this test on CRAN servers? I tried adding `tests\^spelling` to `.Rbuildignore` file, but the test still runs on CRAN. It iwill be good to have defaults that avoid this issue altogether. Because, as pointed out by CRAN members, spellings are not changing on a daily basis and this is a waste computational resources.

title: Allow user to decline to overwrite existing file, from use_template()
description:
Currently `use_template` throws an error when one chooses not to overwrite an existing file:
 
```
usethis::use_template(template = "CONTRIBUTING.md")
Overwrite pre-existing file 'CONTRIBUTING.md'?
1: Absolutely
2: No
3: Not now
 
Selection: 3
Error: 'CONTRIBUTING.md' already exists.
```
Is there any appetite for a PR that would add a `allow_existing` argument (or whatever the name) to `use_template`? So that is, if a file already exists and the `allow_existing` argument is set to `TRUE`, and a user selects to not overwrite (at the prompt), `use_template` simply outputs a 'CONTRIBUTING.md' already exists' warning rather than an error?
 
The context is that we have a series of templates (CoC, README, etc) where a user, when setting up a project or package, may accept the template for some and keep existing files for others. Since `use_template` via `write_over` throws an error, this [type of process where sequential asking which files need to be overwritten](https://github.com/bcgov/bcgovr/issues/37
)  is currently not possible.

title: Option to automatically run `use_data()` code in `/data_raw/` during BUILD and CHECK?
description:
This is as much a package workflow question as a code question, so please forgive if I'm thinking about this the wrong way. 

I really like the transparency of the package creation process where R scripts to generate `/data/foo.rda` files live in `/data_raw/generate_foo.R`. This means another user can see exactly how the `data(foo)` object was generated. 

But, there seems to be a weakness in the process: if you don't run the updated script, the `data(foo)` object will be out of sync with the `/data_raw/generate_foo.R` file. 

One option (mimic'ing `testthat`) is to have all `data_raw/generate-{x}.R` files run during BUILD or CHECK. Perhaps like roxygen there can be some intelligence about only running files with changes (I'm getting our of my depth here.) 

So, this would be more an option for BUILD or CHECK commands, but I wanted to see what others thought first. 🤓🙇

title: Feature Request: use_readme_rmd specifies a different fig.path for R pacakges
description:
Hello!

Thank you again for writing `usethis`! I use it almost every day.

Using `use_readme_rmd()` creates the following YAML and setup code chunk:

````
---
output: github_document
---

<!-- README.md is generated from README.Rmd. Please edit that file -->

```{r, echo = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.path = "README-"
)
```
````

However when using this in an R package, I I borrowed this trick from the [tidyverse packages](https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/blob/master/README.Rmd) to change the `fig.path` to place the figures inside a `man/figures/` folder, like so: 

````
```{r, echo = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.path = "man/figures/README-"
)
```
````

I was wondering if it would be possible for this to be the default when using `use_readme_rmd()` - perhaps there could be a way for it to sense if it is inside an R package, and then change the `fig.path` accordingly?

Just an idea!

title: use_spell_check() should run spelling test conditionally
description:
On my Windows VM, where the Suggested spelling package is not installed, `R CMD check` fails like so:

``` r
* checking tests ...
  Running 'spelling.R'
Warning message:
running command '"C:/PROGRA~1/R/R-34~1.3/bin/x64/R" CMD BATCH --vanilla  "spelling.R" "spelling.Rout"' had status 1 
 ERROR
Running the tests in 'tests/spelling.R' failed.
Complete output:
  > spelling::spell_check_test(vignettes = TRUE, error = FALSE)
  Error in loadNamespace(name) : there is no package called 'spelling'
  Calls: :: ... tryCatch -> tryCatchList -> tryCatchOne -> <Anonymous>
  Execution halted
```

This reveals that `use_spell_check()` should put the spelling test behind `requireNamespace()`.

That is `tests/spelling.R` should look like so:

``` r
if (requireNamespace("spelling", quietly = TRUE)) {
  spelling::spell_check_test(vignettes = TRUE, error = FALSE)
}
```

title: Request: create_citation
description:
*@karlropkins commented on May 16, 2018, 7:22 AM UTC:*

(Seems wrong posting a feature request to an issues site but not sure where else to go with this... sorry if wrong...)

Could you have a create_citation()?

create() makes your package skeleton. That makes DESCRIPTION template using create_description (and build_description). Once the user has updated the DESCRIPTION, they have to make CITATION, but unless they have anything special to document (which tends to come later) that is the manual, and you can extract a preliminary version of that from DESCRIPTION. Adding a create_citation() would save users wanting that minimal CITATION a transpose job and mean even new users would have provisional CITATION in place.

Guessing you would break it into a create_ and build_citation and use functions available through devtools, but I think the process is do-able, e.g.:

`
create_citation <- function (pkg = ".", overwrite = FALSE)
{

#check package, inst and CITATION are useable...
.pkg <- as.package(pkg)
test <- file.path(.pkg$path, c("R", "src", "data"))
if (!any(file.exists(test))) {
stop("'", pkg,
"' does not look like a package: no R/, src/ or data directories",
call. = FALSE)
}
if (!file.exists(file.path(.pkg$path, "inst")))
dir.create(file.path(.pkg$path, "inst"))
if (file.exists(file.path(.pkg$path, "inst/CITATION")))
if(overwrite){
file.remove(file.path(.pkg$path, "inst/CITATION"))
} else {
stop("'", pkg, "' already has CITATION", call. = FALSE)
}

#get citation info
pkg <- .pkg$package #pkg name from description
#if pkg name in title use as is else pkg: title
title <- if(length(grep(pkg, .pkg$title))>0) .pkg$title else
paste(pkg, ": ", .pkg$title, sep="")
#if date in decription use that else use this year
year <- if("date" %in% names(.pkg))
format(as.Date(.pkg$date), "%Y") else
format(Sys.Date(), "%Y")
#make manual and text authors records
authors <- paste(format(eval(parse(text = .pkg$`authors@r`)),
include = c("given", "family")))
txt.aut <- paste(authors, collapse=", ")
txt.aut <- paste(" textVersion = paste("", txt.aut, " (", year,
") ",", sep ="")
if(length(authors)>1)
txt.aut <- gsub(paste(", ", authors[length(authors)], sep=""),
paste(" and ", authors[length(authors)], sep=""),
txt.aut)
man.aut <- paste("as.person("", authors, "")", sep="")
man.aut[1] <- paste(" author = personList(",
man.aut[1], ",", sep="")
if(length(man.aut)>1)
man.aut[2:length(man.aut)] <- paste(" ",
man.aut[2:length(man.aut)], ",",
sep="")
man.aut[length(man.aut)] <- gsub("[)],$", ")),", man.aut[length(man.aut)])

#make a citation template
#note no longer strictly template
#pre-formatting authors details...
out <- c(
"citHeader("To cite '[packname]' package in publications use:")",
"",
"citEntry(entry="Manual",",
" title = "[packtitle]",",
man.aut,
" year = "[year]",",
" note = paste("R package version ",",
" packageDescription("[packname]",",
" fields = c("Version"))[1], sep=""),",
txt.aut,
" "[packtitle], ",",
" "R package version ",",
" packageDescription("[packname]",",
" fields = c("Version"))[1],".", sep=""))",
"",
"citFooter("Please cite both '[packname]' and R ",",
" "when using '[packname]'.",",
" "For R citation, see ", sQuote("citation()"))"
)

#update template
out <- gsub("[[]packname[]]", pkg, out)
out <- gsub("[[]packtitle[]]", title, out)
out <- gsub("[[]year[]]", year, out)

#make CITATION
fileConn<-file(file.path(.pkg$path, "inst/CITATION"), "at")
writeLines(out, fileConn)
close(fileConn)
}
`

*This issue was moved by [jimhester](https://github.com/jimhester) from [r-lib/devtools#1782](https://github.com/r-lib/devtools/issues/1782).*

title: Refactor use_course()
description:
Some code shared by @jeroen in a Slack conversation about `use_course()`

``` r
library(curl)

download_with_cd <- function(url, destdir = "."){
  h <- new_handle(noprogress = FALSE)
  tmp <- tempfile()
  curl::curl_fetch_disk(url, tmp, handle = h)
  headers <- curl::parse_headers_list(handle_data(h)$headers)
  filename <- stringr::str_match(headers[["content-disposition"]], "filename=.*")[1]
  filename <- sub("filename=", "", filename)
  outfile <- normalizePath(file.path(destdir, filename), mustWork = FALSE)
  file.rename(tmp, outfile)
  return(outfile)
}

download_with_cd("https://cran.ocpu.io/ggplot2/data/diamonds/csv", destdir = "~")
```

Other notes:

  * If you use `curl_fetch_disk` you can check the `status` code also from `handle_data()`.
  * Using `curl_download()` might be easier -- automatically throws an error if the result is not http 200
  * the trick is all functions in curl take a handle, and you can always use `handle_data()` to access the metadata after the request

title: use_github does not push with https protocol and GITHUB_PAT
description:
I tried to create a 📦 with `usethis` calling at some point `use_github`. 

First my setup is: 
* Windows
* GITHUB_PAT environment variable is written in `.Renviron`
* I get correct results from `gh::gh_whoami`.

Howerver, when using https protocol, `use_github` does not manage to push to the created repo because of a mishandling of credential with git2r. 

Here how to reproduce the issue

``` r
testdir <- tempfile("testdir")
dir.create(testdir)
setwd(testdir)
library(usethis)
#> Warning: le package 'usethis' a été compilé avec la version R 3.4.4
create_package("testpkg", open = FALSE)
#> Changing active project to testpkg
#> <U+2714> Creating 'R/'
#> <U+2714> Creating 'man/'
#> <U+2714> Writing 'DESCRIPTION'
#> <U+2714> Writing 'NAMESPACE'
setwd(file.path(testdir, "testpkg/"))
use_git()
#> <U+2714> Initialising Git repo
#> <U+2714> Adding '.Rhistory', '.RData', '.Rproj.user' to './.gitignore'
#> <U+2714> Adding files and committing
use_github(protocol = "https")
#> <U+2714> Setting title and description
#>   Name:        testpkg
#>   Description: What the Package Does (One Line, Title Case)
#> <U+2714> Creating GitHub repository
#> <U+2714> Adding GitHub remote
#> <U+2714> Adding GitHub links to DESCRIPTION
#> <U+2714> Setting URL field in DESCRIPTION to 'https://github.com/cderv/testpkg'
#> <U+2714> Setting BugReports field in DESCRIPTION to 'https://github.com/cderv/testpkg/issues'
#> <U+2714> Pushing to GitHub and setting remote tracking branch
#> Error in (function (classes, fdef, mtable) : unable to find an inherited method for function 'cred_user_pass' for signature '"character", "NULL"'
```

the last step failed. The repository was created but use\_github was not able to push to the repository. It seems it can’t deal with current git2r credential.  

https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/blob/7d1c255f7983b2bcda050e74b73f3d830b3a79da/R/github.R#L142-L147

The credentials used are built with `cred <- git2r::cred_user_pass("EMAIL", auth_token)`.
However, here `auth_token = NULL` by default and `git2r` does not know how to handle that.
`auth_token = NULL` by default indicates in the documentation that it should use the github PAT.
I am really not sure to understand why the use of `cred_user_pass` with `"EMAIL"` as username and an `auth_token` as password. I will try to investigate further the reason of this choice, but if you have an explanation, please tell me.

As it seems strange to me I tried another way.   
First, `git2r` as specific credential object for token authentification, that by default get the `GITHUB_PAT` environment variable. Using this works.

``` r
r <- git2r::repository(file.path(testdir, "testpkg/"))
cred <- git2r::cred_token()
git2r::push(r, "origin", "refs/heads/master", credentials = cred)
```

There is also a way to use user/pass auth with the token using the username (or organization) and token as password.

``` r
cred2 <- git2r::cred_user_pass("cderv", Sys.getenv("GITHUB_PAT"))
# nothing to push but no error
git2r::push(r, "origin", "refs/heads/master", credentials = cred)

# cleaning this reprex
unlink(testdir, recursive = TRUE)

# delete manually the repo on github
```

A the end, do you think the choice in `use_github` is correct ? Should it be change to another credential object ? What are you thinking about all this ? 

I am wiling to help with a PR when ready. Thanks.

title: usethis CRAN needs git2r dev version
description:
Working on #320, I encounter an issue with one `git2r` function.

https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/blob/9ab0e799e2c092913f74a4e3d55f893e266d99cc/R/github.R#L148-L150

This was a change to take into account new behavior in dev version of `git2r`. However, `utils::head` throws an error with CRAN version of `git2r`.
``` r
testdir <- tempfile("testdir")
dir.create(testdir)
dir_path <- file.path(testdir, "testpkg")
packageVersion("git2r")
#> [1] '0.21.0'
packageVersion("usethis")
#> [1] '1.3.0'
usethis::create_package(dir_path, open = FALSE)
#> Changing active project to testpkg
#> <U+2714> Creating 'R/'
#> <U+2714> Creating 'man/'
#> <U+2714> Writing 'DESCRIPTION'

#> <U+2714> Adding files and committing
repo <- git2r::repository(dir_path)
git2r::head(repo)
#> [d499db] (Local) (HEAD) master
utils::head(repo)
#> Error in x[seq_len(n)]: objet de type 'S4' non indiçable
unlink(testdir, recursive = T)
```
Created on 2018-04-22 by the [reprex package](http://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.2.0).

Moreover, in new dev version of git2r, `head.git_repository` is [deprecated](https://github.com/ropensci/git2r/commit/4602da9c22b7afeed323f081bf7c53064bb6a09e). A [new ](https://github.com/ropensci/git2r/commit/24019226b771b10b5ccda48e1fece5880cc6ddbe) `repository_head` should be used now.

``` r
testdir <- tempfile("testdir")
dir.create(testdir)
dir_path <- file.path(testdir, "testpkg")
devtools::dev_mode(on = TRUE)
#> Dev mode: ON
packageVersion("git2r")
#> [1] '0.21.0.9002'
packageVersion("usethis")
#> [1] '1.3.0'
usethis::create_package(dir_path, open = FALSE)
#> Changing active project to testpkg
#> <U+2714> Creating 'R/'
#> <U+2714> Creating 'man/'
#> <U+2714> Writing 'DESCRIPTION'
#> <U+2714> Writing 'NAMESPACE'
withr::with_dir(dir_path, usethis::use_git())
#> <U+2714> Initialising Git repo
#> <U+2714> Adding '.Rhistory', '.RData', '.Rproj.user' to './.gitignore'
#> <U+2714> Adding files and committing
repo <- git2r::repository(dir_path)
git2r::head(repo)
#> Error: 'head' n'est pas un objet exporté depuis 'namespace:git2r'
utils::head(repo)
#> Warning: 'head.git_repository' est obsolète.
#> Utilisez plutôt 'repository_head'
#> Voir help("Deprecated")
#> [7472f5] (Local) (HEAD) master
git2r::repository_head(repo)
#> [7472f5] (Local) (HEAD) master
unlink(testdir, recursive = T)
```

Created on 2018-04-22 by the [reprex package](http://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.2.0).

This line of code is currently inside the code I am modifying for the PR I am working on to fix #320. 
I am thinking of fixing also this. Would you prefer another PR instead ? 

Moreover, shouldn't CRAN usethis sticks with git2r CRAN version behaviour (0.21.0) until next git2r version arrives on CRAN ? concretely, should I use `git2r::head` or `git2r::repository_head` ? 
This fix is need in order for `use_github` to work properly and be correctly tested (part of #322 that I also will try to contribute to)

Thanks for your direction.

title: Proposal: README_to_vignette()
description:
As per the contributing guide, I'm posting an issue as a preface to a PR.

I've been working towards a goal of increasing vignette usage and part of that has been [volunteering to write some](https://twitter.com/carroll_jono/status/961139524901527552). I've noticed along the way that  while many packages might lack a vignette, they do tend to have a rather nice/complete rendered `README.md` file. This achieves a certain goal: that new users should see what the package does from the GitHub landing page. The downsides being that this file is not visible from the installed package itself, and that there is not guarantee that the `README` is not stale due to recent updates. A vignette is likely a more suitable place for this content, but users have either chosen not to use one or are not aware how to do so.

I propose a new function in `usethis` which converts an existing `README.Rmd` file to a proper vignette (as best as can be automated). This isn't a complete solution: the user would still need to edit this file, but it significantly lowers the barrier to entry. I feel that `usethis` is the right home for this function, alongside the usual `use_vignette()` functionality.

The second part of this would be teaching users how to source part or all of a vignette from the `README.Rmd` file using the `child` option from `knitr`: https://www.garrickadenbuie.com/blog/2018/03/05/dry-vignette-and-readme/ 

The benefit of this enabled workflow is that the vignette stays with the package, the `README` still contains the relevant information, updates still only need to occur in one place, and testing is performed on the example code on installation.

**I seek the `usethis` maintainers' input on whether or not this would be a welcome PR. [It is ready to go, here](https://github.com/r-lib/usethis/compare/master...jonocarroll:feature-README-to-vignette?expand=1).**

For additional context, [I have processed](https://github.com/jonocarroll/VolunteerVignettes) several packages' `README` files into suitable vignettes as tests: 

* [r-lib/fs](https://jonocarroll.github.io/VolunteerVignettes/fs/fs-README-vignette.html)

* [shabbychef/mazealls](https://jonocarroll.github.io/VolunteerVignettes/mazealls/mazealls-README-vignette.html)

* [thomasp85/patchwork](https://jonocarroll.github.io/VolunteerVignettes/patchwork/patchwork-README-vignette.html)

* [alexpghayes/formulize](https://jonocarroll.github.io/VolunteerVignettes/formulize/formulize-README-vignette.html)

* [ThinkR-open/remedy](https://jonocarroll.github.io/VolunteerVignettes/remedy/remedy-README-vignette.html) (large file size warning; lots of embedded gifs)

title: On Windows, pasting the badge code into an Rmd causes a pandoc error
description:
I don't think the root cause of this bug is in `usethis`, but I'm documenting a workaround until somebody can trace the root cause.

The standard procedure of using a badge, e.g. `usethis::use_lifecycle_badge()` is to paste the resulting snippet into the `README.md` or `README.Rmd`.

However, on Windows, using the badge in an `.Rmd` file causes a pandoc error:

```
pandoc.exe: Could not fetch https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg
TlsExceptionHostPort (HandshakeFailed Error_EOF) "img.shields.io" 443
Error: pandoc document conversion failed with error 67
In addition: Warning message:
running command '"C:/Program Files/RStudio/bin/pandoc/pandoc" +RTS -K512m -RTS README.md --to html4 --from markdown_github-ascii_identifiers --output README.html --standalone --self-contained --highlight-style pygments --template "C:\Users\apdev\Documents\R\win-library\3.4\rmarkdown\rmarkdown\templates\github_document\resources\preview.html" --variable "github-markdown-css:C:\Users\apdev\Documents\R\win-library\3.4\rmarkdown\rmarkdown\templates\github_document\resources\github.css" --email-obfuscation none' had status 67 
Execution halted
```

The workaround is to not paste the badge snippet directly in the markdown, but to create a chunk with `results='asis'`, and the paste the badge snippet inside a `cat()` statement in the chunk.  For example:

```r

 ```{r echo=FALSE, prompt=FALSE, results='asis', comment=""}
cat('
[![lifecycle](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://www.tidyverse.org/lifecycle/#experimental)
')
    ```

```

A similar issue was filed on the `badgecreatr` project at https://github.com/RMHogervorst/badgecreatr/issues/25, where the suggestion is to add `<!-- rmarkdown v1 -->` to the top of the `.Rmd`.  This doesn't work for me.

title: Tools facilitating reproducible analysis
description:
This is not technically an issue but more a ping to see if there would be any interest in a feature(s)...

There is a lot of interest at the moment in the scientific community to facilitate reproducible analysis and it seems that using R packages are, in some ways, an optimal solution (see e.g. [template](https://github.com/Pakillo/template)). Despite this, there are some challenges when utilising R packages for this purpose, such as reproducing the environment in which the analysis was done (i.e. mostly package versions). Some tools like docker, [liftr](https://liftr.me), and others have provided a lot of help in accomplishing this but, in my opinion, the workflow could be more stream lined/automated to make the process easier. This is where I think usethis could be useful. 

Although I have not had the opportunity to extensively review different options (such as [checkpoint](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/checkpoint/index.html)), my current workflow uses liftr and docker to reproduce my analysis working environment. liftr uses a .yml file from which a docker file is produced. This is then used to recreate the working environment before rendering .Rmd files containing analyses. I have a quick and dirty example at: [reproducibleAnalysis](https://github.com/jasonserviss/reproducibleAnalysis) showing how I utilise these two tools. My thought was that usethis could have a "use_liftr" command that sets up the liftr .yml file dependant on what packages are currently loaded when the analysis takes place. Potentially there are other liftr/docker processes that could also be automated.

There may be better ways to reproduce a working environment and if there is any interest in facilitating reproducible analysis with usethis I could try to put some time into looking into this further although it is a bit unclear if this idea would fit into the primary goals for the usethis package.

Minor issue from #109

If any behavior doesn't need auth, then it should work without this, otherwise, it should be documented that you should set `GITHUB_PAT` as an env var, and the function should probably have an argument to specify the token directly, consistent with `use_github()` etc.

title: use_github needs option to switch repos
description:
Followup from #109 

`use_github()` should be able to update the the git remote `origin` in an existing repository to point to the specified GitHub repository; creating said GitHub repository if necessary.  This would support the use case of cloning a template repo from GitHub and then establishing a new repository, with new name and potentially new org/user, on GitHub, as the remote.  


----

@hadley I think the above captures what you suggested in #109, but I'm not entirely sure.  There's clearly a couple of rather distinct patterns here and it's not obvious to me how best to divide or modularize them across the `usethis` API.  e.g. a partial list (cc @jennybc who also thinks about this more clearly than me!):

- Starting a new project from scratch / RStudio new->project menu and syncing to GitHub (compare to classic workflow of creating blank repo on GitHub first, then initializing project boilerplate).
- Starting a new project from a template repo, giving it a new name and syncing to new location on GitHub (Compare this to what GitHub Classroom does with template repos)
- Forking a project (identical to GitHub fork)
- Forking a project without registering as a Fork
- 

Clearly these are related to both `use_github` an `create_github_repo` functionality, but it's not clear if each is best done with it's own function or with a combination of modular functions.  Apologies if I'm getting derailed again in mixing issues.

title: Location of user-level git dotfiles on Windows
description:
From AppVeyor and my Windows VM, I gather that user's `.gitconfig` and `.gitignore` are typically not in what R regards as user's home directory. On my VM:

``` r
as.list(Sys.getenv(
  c("HOME", "R_USER", "HOMEDRIVE", "HOMEPATH", "USERPROFILE")
))
#> $HOME
#> [1] "C:/Users/JennyVM/Documents"
#> 
#> $R_USER
#> [1] "C:/Users/JennyVM/Documents"
#> 
#> $HOMEDRIVE
#> [1] "C:"
#> 
#> $HOMEPATH
#> [1] "\\Users\\JennyVM"
#> 
#> $USERPROFILE
#> [1] "C:\\Users\\JennyVM"

normalizePath("~")
#> [1] "C:\\Users\\JennyVM\\Documents"

list.files(Sys.getenv("USERPROFILE"), all.files = TRUE, pattern = "git", full.names = TRUE)
#> [1] "C:\\Users\\JennyVM/.gitconfig"
```

Home directory is `C:/Users/USER/Documents` but user's git dot files are one level up, in `C:/Users/USER`. I see the same on AppVeyor. I have accepted default git setup everywhere.

`edit_git_config("user")` and `edit_git_ignore("user")` should be adjusted accordingly, for Windows. Currently they seek/put these files in the home directory. This new config file then seems to mask the pre-existing one, causing, e.g., `user.name` and `user.email` to be appear to be unset.

title: Add AppVeyor
How to develop with `withr::defer()`
description:
@hadley added this function, presumably because it's handy in the tests:

``` r
scoped_temporary_package <- function(dir = tempfile(), env = parent.frame()) {
  old <- proj$cur
  withr::defer(proj_set(old), envir = env)

  utils::capture.output(create_package(dir, rstudio = FALSE, open = FALSE))
  invisible(dir)
}
```

But when you're *developing* the test, you can't actually call `scoped_temporary_package()`. You get this:

```
 Error in withr::defer(proj_set(old), envir = env) : 
  attempt to defer event on global environment 
```

Which makes life rather difficult. I think I've run up against this in some other recent experiment with `withr::defer()`. What to do? Is there something that could or should be different about `withr::defer()`? Or should I finesse this inside `scoped_temporary_package()`?

cc @jimhester

title: Consider use_repo_template function?
description:
usethis has great utilities for setting up a vanilla template using `create_package()`, along with `use_git()`, `use_github()` , as @jennybc describes in https://community.rstudio.com/t/procedure-to-create-a-project-for-a-package-destined-for-github/2054/4.

But this [twitter thread](https://twitter.com/bearloga/status/926990297422225408) got me thinking: often rather start with my own template: don't have to enter my name, choose my usual license, and other tweaks.  Moreover, sometimes my template isn't a package, but a more minimal [project repo](https://github.com/cboettig/compendium); or maybe it's a specific template for some classroom assignment I want students to use.  

It would be nice to have a function to deploy some existing template repo.   e.g. this is basically what GitHub forking does, without creating the 'fork' connection, and allowing a new repo name.  (Similar also to what GitHub Classroom does, but that's bound to a single organization destination).  

I think this would be a straight-forward wrapper around existing `git2r` / command-line git calls to rename the remote origin; possibly with a `gh` wrapper (or just single github API call via httr to avoid the dependency?) to create the new repo on GitHub.  I sketched a prototype of this here: https://github.com/cboettig/template/blob/master/R/template.R. Would be happy to send a PR if something along these lines makes sense, though no doubt the `usethis` team could manage a more robust implementation more efficiently anyhow, if it's worth doing.  

Thanks for your thoughts.

I have written a wrapper function which initialises a new package with infrastructure and then switches to the new RStudio project in a new RStudio session. However, as a side-effect, all the files mentioned above get opened in my old RStudio session.
It would be nice to be able to pass an `open = FALSE` argument to the underlying code. For example, here is the code for use_package_doc:

```R
function (pkg = ".") 
{
    pkg <- as.package(pkg)
    use_template("packagename-package.r", file.path("R", paste(pkg$package, 
        "-package.r", sep = "")), data = list(name = pkg$package), 
        open = TRUE, pkg = pkg)
}
<environment: namespace:devtools>
```

Note the `open = TRUE` on the fourth line of function body code, which seems to be an argument of the internal {devtools} function devtools:::use_template. Perhaps this argument could be exposed to users of the higher-level functions.

title: Automate CRAN full license text workaround
description:
Currently the [R-exts guidelines](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-exts.html#Licensing) discourage package authors from including the full license text in the source repository (see https://github.com/tidyverse/tidyr/issues/262). However, this is problematic as repositories are major points of distribution.

While CRAN seemed unlikely to change their policies, there is a simple workaround implemented in https://github.com/tidyverse/tidyr/pull/267. @hadley suggested I open an issue here to create a "standard helper so that this is automated".

title: Handle host for use_github() same way as auth_token
description: **Issue by [jennybc](https://github.com/jennybc)** _Wednesday Sep 07, 2016 at 23:33 GMT_ _Originally opened as https://github.com/hadley/devtools/issues/1333_ ---- I propose handling the host for `use_github()` in a similar fashion as `auth_token`, which is this: - by default, helper function `github_pat()` is called, which tries to retrieve PAT from env var GITHUB_PAT Could we use an env var named GITHUB_API_URL for this? I suggest it because [`gh`](https://github.com/gaborcsardi/gh) already [does this](https://github.com/gaborcsardi/gh/blob/b7d3b8071ab24c67fd6db10f2997b3ab9d5f612d/R/package.R#L94). If GITHUB_API_URL is not defined, then use existing default `https://api.github.com`. This makes it easier to define a user-level GITHUB_PAT for github.com and, for individual projects, store an alternative host and PAT for GitHub Enterprise in a project-level `.Renviron`. cc @ijlyttle

title: update .gitignore in vignettes folder with `use_vignette()`?
description:
(migrated from https://github.com/hadley/devtools/issues/1547)

To ignore .R and .html files generated when knitting .Rmd documents. This is desired because calls to e.g.

    devtools::document(roclets = "vignette")

will drop the generated `.R` and `.html` files within the `vignettes` folder after completion. Note that RStudio users can opt-in to having this roclet run on Build and Reload within the IDE, so it's likely that such users will have these files sitting in the `vignettes` folder after a package build.
